The soup comes with a strange yet tasty bread, deli meat and spicy mustard The cheese fondue had a beer flavor to it that was unique. Must try.  For the main meal we had sausage and sauerkraut.  The sauerkraut was mixed with potato...I think and was amazing. I would like to go back and try the meatball instead of the sausage next time.  The sausage was a link and not my favorite.The staff was so kind and inviting.Jack

Name: Mia L.
Review: The Pantry was the last meal we had in Amsterdam and it was the best! The service was great, the food was delicious, and the beer was fantastic. The interior was beautiful.

Name: Briana B.
Review: Amazing experience! We didn't have a reservation but the host was extremely nice and squeezed us in. Food was delicious and service was perfect!

Name: Kathleen F.
Review: What an unexpected treat! We wanted traditional Dutch food and the pantry was just that. What was even better was the cheerful, fun, super easy-going staff. These folks were fabulous!

Name: Adi A.
Review: We came here esecially and it was really nice (:Good dutch food, good vibe and the owner is super sweet

Name: Ruben G.
Review: We had split pea soup (and a few other things) and it was the best soup we've ever had. So good. The other food was great as well. They brew their own beer and it was excellent as well. Service was very nice. Multilingual menus as well.

Name: Stephen T.
Review: What an amazing dining experience we had. Very traditional Dutch food with vegetarian options. The menu comes in many languages and the service was outstanding! Warm comfort food in a cozy space. Highly recommended.

Name: Beau F.
Review: Wow, this place is just so real and authentic. Really great Dutch food, felt like I was eating at my Dutch grandmother's house. As K and I were here on a chilly winter night, this was perfect! Here's what we got:Cold starter: combination of 3 Dutch sausages. These were great, real local sausages. Yum.Combination of hutspot, boerenkoolstamppot and zuurkoolstamppot (served with a smoked sausage or a meatball): oh god, this was just amazing. Just get it. It's rich, complex, and crazy filling. I could eat my weight in this dish.Savoury beef and onion stew(with red cabbage and mashed potatoes): k loves stews. She's Irish. As stews go, this was great, but you gotta dig on stew. Super authentic and tasty if this is your deal, so can't knock it.I loved the staff here, too. So nice. I'd come back here in a heartbeat. They are busy so I'd recommend calling ahead for a reservation!

Name: Pete M.
Review: I ate the beef and onion stew with red cabbage and mashed potatoes. My boyfriend had the "oven dish" (like a cauliflower, cheese, potatoes and beef hot plate). Our appetizer was bitterballen. Our total ticket price was 45 dollars. The menue was available in like 8 languages. The staff was friendly. The food was perfect for the price.

Name: Tim X.
Review: I was visiting Amsterdam for a few days with family and we were looking for quality, traditional Dutch food. I'm so glad we found the Pantry. The first night we came, they were fully booked, so we made a reservation for the following evening. Definitely make a rezzo if you're going for weekend dinner!We ordered all the classics: the shrimp croquettes, split pea soup, Dutch sausages combo with bread, and the sausage with 3 types of mashed potatoes. Everything was delicious and well prepared. A few of the Dutch sausages were unique tasting--I think one was liver? And the shrimp croquettes were on the smaller side, but that's nitpicking. We also ordered the seabass fillet, which was good, but not quite on the same level as the other dishes. Maybe should have gone for the Dutch steak instead.The atmosphere is very cozy inside, tables are quite close together but not uncomfortable. Service is very friendly, all the waiters speak English and provide English menus. Customers appeared to be a good mix of locals and tourists, so you know it's not a tourist trap!Would definitely recommend this place for dinner to anyone visiting Amsterdam looking for authentic Dutch food.

Name: Steve F.
Review: The host, Bas is just amazing!! Friendly, efficient, and in perpetual motion.  Whatever the owner pays him is not enough.          And the food? Just sensational.  Traditional Dutch comfort food - sausages, mashed potatoes, the most delicious red cabbage prepared with wine and brown sugar.  WOW!!      If you are looking for authentic Dutch food in Amsterdam, The Pantry is the place!!

Name: Lilian K.
Review: I love the people who run this restaurant; the place is decorated very nicely and is a bit small so remember to make a reservation if you plan on coming during peak dinner times.For us, we arrived around 5:30 and the woman gladly took us in even without a reservation. She was so friendly and energetic! The man serving us as well was kind enough to explain what items were on the dish since we clearly were tourists who were trying a traditional Dutch meal for the first time.I ordered the combination plate with a meatball (3 types of mash with sauerkraut, kale, and a blend of beef/carrot/onion). All three mashes were so so good. The meat ball was also delicious as well.I'm glad to have had a nice setting sit down meal with food that I can trust to be traditional.

Name: Dan A.
Review: We were visiting Amsterdam and wanted to have an authentic Dutch dinner.  The Pantry didn't disappoint!  This is the ultimate comfort food!  We started with the Shrimp Croquettes which we really didn't need as the entree portions are more than enough.  We decided to split the Dutch Ham (a visual as well as culinary experience and be warned-huge!) and the combo Hutspot (mashed potatoes) with sausage and added meatball was excellent!  We had the La Trappe Quadrupel Ale which is a Dutch (Belgian style) Ale & was very good.  The Pantry is charming, cozy & small (& they do get busy) so reservations are highly recommended (especially if planning on going during peak times).  Service was also excellent!

Name: Emma C.
Review: Excellent service and food! You can't really go wrong with Dutch home cooking. The pea soup was delightful! I got the meatball with three different types of mash potatoes as my entree and I loved every part of it. The wait staff was also very friendly and spoke English, so that was a plus!

Name: Yalena R.
Review: Excellent service and really Dutch food!!! Exquisite Good price and quality food!!!You wanted to this place

Name: Kim l.
Review: Delicious Dutch food! I found this place on yelp and told hubby to meet me there after the RAI conference. We were seated outside on the patio in an alley. I ordered their special which included one sausage and mashed potatoes prepared in 3 different ways. Everything was delicious. Hubby ordered steak with veggies. He enjoyed his dish. I ordered a split pea soup and my kids devoured it. The dessert yogurt dessert was yummy too. Service was efficient and friendly. They had a problem processing our credit card for some odd reason so we had to pay with cash. When we were leaving a family was looking at the menu and I told them that the food was fantastic so they quickly took a seat outside. However the waiter came and told them that all the seats were reserved already. Wow...good thing we came when we did!

Name: Rebecca T.
Review: If you want delicious traditional Dutch food with cute decor and friendly service, this is the spot! Thanks to yelp, we were able to locate our next food adventure. Of course in the Netherlands, you'll have to try Dutch food!We got the famous dish... Potatoes. The ménage à trois of mashed potatoes will offer you the most interesting flavor profile you can have - sauerkraut, kale and sweet potato/carrots/onions! All three tasted amazing with great flavors and the right amount of richness. Some mashed I had was way too buttery and it gets gross. Not this one. We also had the beef stew and goodness it was so tender and delicious! I cleaned my plate and so did he!It's also a great place to try some local Dutch beer! The only disappointing thing was the yogurt/parfait kind of dessert. It was a bit to melty and nasty. We didn't finish it. The decor was very cute with a lot of different lamps by the door and their famous Delftware on the wall. All the staff there were friendly too and were proud of what they served. We had a great evening there!

Name: Chris L.
Review: Our hotel staff recommended we check out The Pantry for Dutch food, and we were glad we did.  The food was great.  I can't even remember what we got, but the staff were really friendly and everything tasted wonderful.  We tried a sampling of foods and it was all very good.  We'd definitely come back here again.

Name: Jane C.
Review: Must visit when in Amsterdam! We made reservations in advance and happy we did. The restaurant was packed at 6 pm! Service is super quick and friendly. Food was amazing!

Name: Conrad B.
Review: Visited 09/15/2018Stopped in for a traditional Dutch meal and weren't disappointedI had their #1 special which was pea soup with bacon (excellent!) and a couple of Hutspots. Hutspots are mashed potatoes mixed with different veggies. In my case one was mixed with kale, one with sour kraut and one with carrots and onions. I like the mashed potatoes with carrots and onions the best. My wife had the sea bass with veggies and mashed potatoes which she enjoyed. This restaurants is in the middle of 10,000 restaurants. The whole area is really one massive 'hangout.' You won't go hungry if you're lost in this area of Amsterdam.

Name: Carin L.
Review: Most delicious food in Amsterdam I think I've tasted! The food was cooked perfectly.  Defyingly a go to place for authentic Dutch cuisine! We made reservations a few days ahead which is a much in order to get a seat.  Highly recommend!

Name: Charlotte S.
Review: First time traditional Dutch cuisine I was impressed with combination of flavors. Well balanced portions from Starters to Dessert. Nice atmosphere can see why it had so many 5 star reviews.

Name: Kimberly C.
Review: Our hotel staff recommended we check out The Pantry for Dutch food, and we were glad we did.  The food was great.  I can't even remember what we got, but the staff were really friendly and everything tasted wonderful.  We tried a sampling of foods and it was all very good.  We'd definitely come back here again.

Name: David K.
Review: Customer service was excellent!!! My friend is a vegetarian and they made sure to cater a traditional Hutspot Dutch meal to her. The food was delicious. For the rest of us meat eaters, we ordered the Hutspot combination and bitterballen. Traditional Dutch food at its finest!!

Name: Karen M.
Review: Simply excellent. The fried goat cheese was amazing. I also enjoyed a delicious sausage dish that could also be served as a meatball. Highly recommend.

Name: Tammi F.
Review: We were staying in Amsterdam and wanted to try actual Dutch food. We ended up coming back here afterward because we wanted to try other things on the menu! Fantastic experience, lovely waitstaff and we were very happy with the food. Definitely the best place in the area.

Name: Louis R.
Review: Awesome! Delicious food and friendly, welcoming service! My wife and I both had halibut and it was seared to perfection.Highly recommended!

Name: Brenda E.
Review: I read about Van Speyk and reserved a table prior to our visit. No walk-in service is available and rightfully so. The food was carefully prepared and the presentation was beautiful. Each dish we had was delicious and the experience was amazing! Try the dark chocolate creme brulee!

Name: Michael S.
Review: Service, meal prep and presentation was excellent.  We had the fillet and the halibut, both were delightful.  We were able to get a nice table without a reservation, the historic building is warm and welcoming.  Overall a great experience.

Name: Yc T.
Review: Awesome dinners!!! We waited a while to get our food and it was so delicious. Granted we had 7 people and right after we ordered the restaurant filled up. I've always love eating here. Foods always served hot and not overly salted. It was all perfect! Desserts were awesome as well After all, good meal and good time for us thanks And lastly .... beautiful restaurant with the chandeliers aboveBtw, Jamie is a exceptional waitress! She made our dinner even better

Name: Christina W.
Review: Carpaccio was simply amazing. My husband should be happy I shared any with him.  Escargot was very good as well. Both were the best I've ever had.  The risotto was exceptional. My husband had the tuna and was seared very well. I had a bite and If you like tuna raw, then this is not for you. And last but not least, I had the Dutch dessert, which again, was amazeballs. One of my top ten meals of all time.

Name: Emmie S.
Review: We were looking for a restaurant with authentic Dutch cuisine and the concierge at our hotel recommended this place.  The food and service were both great!!For appetizer I had the Erwtensoep, a traditional Dutch pea soup with smoked sausage and it was delicious!  Totally hit the spot on that freezing cold night!  For dinner I had the Eendenbout which was homemade confit of duck-leg with Dutch potato and sauerkraut mash and orange gravy.  It was perfectly cooked and flavored...everything in the dish complemented each other superbly!  For dessert we shared the Tarte Tatin which was hot apple pie from the oven with a scoop of cinnamon ice cream and it was yummy!!I will definitely dine here again!

Name: Jeff B.
Review: I travel to AMS several times a year, and this is my  go to restaurant. The service is impeccable, and you absolutely have the beef carpaccio - best appetizer I have had in the world.Main dishes can't hold up to the BC, but the filet and the beef stew are both above average.Beautiful building dating to 1700's. Don't hesitate; make your plans here'

Name: Tina Ø.
Review: Superb dinner and very good service - can highly be recommended. We will definitely be back

Name: Koko S.
Review: Amazing too notch place.   Been around for about 7 years per the waiter jP and it shows.  Their menu is remarkable.  I actually walked downstairs in my very happy state to find out who the chef was to tell him how amazing the food was.  While I'm a vegetarian, folks at the table who were not said the escargot and the steak special was hands down the best meal they had in years.   As the sole vegetarian the onion soup and mashed potatoes and mushrooms were so outstanding I plan to go back again tomorrow night as their sides of veggies were better than any other main veggie dish a chef had made us in Amsterdam.  And I've been here over 2 weeks now for work and I would eat here  every night with the same choices each night.

Name: Samuel A.
Review: This place was recommend by the hotel concierge and it did not disappoint.  The staff was polite, professional, and patient.  The I travel with was really happy with our meals. I had the Seafood Risotto and spinach.  The Risotto was cooked to perfection and the shrimps, clams, and scallop were delicious.  I highly recommend you try this Dutch restaurant out if you are in Amsterdam

Name: Kara W.
Review: The atmosphere is AMAZING, the food was spectacular,  and the service was pretty great, too.You have to get the strawberry dessert... it was to die for.

Name: Anelya S.
Review: Went here yesterday for our date night. I picked this place because I liked the decorations and I was right. Its perfect for the date night, if you manage to get a booth and sit next to each other. We had oysters, shrimp crockets, escargot, steak and rack of lamb, the desert of everything and two bottles of Malbec. With tip, it was 220 Euro. Food was solid, service was attentive, and we had a good evening.

Name: jeannette h.
Review: This has to be my favorite spot for escargot, it's buttery and crispy....so good! Mouth water watering, one order is not enough!  All the dishes we ordered were delightful. I had the whole fried sole. It was suggested to me to have the sole fish...great choice! Good flavor and easy to debone.  Fiancé ordered 28day dry aged rib eye...also delicious! Reservations recommended

Name: Rhonda W.
Review: we ate here the night we arrived and it was a lovely start to our trip. The concierge at our hotel   (the Renaissance  which a Marriott hotel)  recommended Van Speyk  .. showed us a menu and called to get us a reservation. We walked right over and were seated immediately which was very impressive on a  Friday night. Our server said it was fortunate that the concierge had called for us. This was my first experience with white asparagus and I LOVED it.          We started with escargot ... and bread.  I had the salmon with white asparagus , mash potatoes. My husband has a lamp chop with veggies .. a potato casserole and something that was like a spicy polenta ... but not sure what it was.  We both had a couple beers and enjoyed our meal. The service was fast and friendly until it came to getting the check and paying.  We found a good deal of the restaurants in Amsterdam  to be VERY slow to give you a check ..  we suspect that since tips aren't as common they aren't in any hurry to get you out of there.            The decor was lovely but the seating was a bit tight .. nice meal ... would recommend.

Name: Diana B.
Review: An amazing dinner. This was suggested by the Double Tree and he was on point.We started with a local beer, the fish platter and pea soup.  They were wonderful along with the atmosphere.  For dinner we had the duck and mussels. Both dishes were amazing.Will be more than happy to return to suck an enjoyable experience.Thanks Joey!

Name: Brittany S.
Review: Wine selection and food was outstanding. Fabulous steak! Cooked and seasoned to perfection.

Name: Jane K.
Review: Great food and incredible service! Checked it out because it was close to the Renaissance Hotel and was probably my favorite meal of my trip in Amsterdam.Even the appetizer bread and butter tasted better than normal. For seafood, try the oysters (bigger and super juicy) or the Dutch sole.For dessert, cheesecake is a must! They forgot to give my dad his coffee, but instead of just removing it from the check, they also served him one on the house.

Name: Brian C.
Review: Was in Amsterdam alone on business and decided to eat here once again... The friendly staff greeted me as I walked in and sat me close to the bar area..: beautiful and massive chandeliers light up the restaurant just enough and the table candles make it a nice spot for a couple - Had the days special 3 course set menu - started with the venison pate - I am not a pate fan but it was delicious !  Then followed by the duck breast and again super delicious - good portion size and great tasting veggies Finished off with a nice light desert !

Name: Bob B.
Review: Went here for Dutch experience and was not disappointed. The waitress Jaime Joy was fantastic very attentive to our needs!  The halibut and seafood risotto did not disappoint. The Van Speyk salad was exceptional. Highly recommend this restaurant

Name: Marcus L.
Review: Great service and amazing food!  I love how they bring bread and menus to each table within a minute of being seated.  The food was excellent and it was one of our best meals here in Amsterdam.  Try the warm waffle dessert!  So delicious!

Name: Michael N.
Review: Excellent evening at Van Speyk. It was recommended by our hotel concierge as we wanted something with good Dutch cuisine. Had the beef stew which was perfect for a cold Amsterdam night. Very friendly and attentive service.

Name: David L.
Review: Great FoieGras. Charming EU style.  It's not typical Dutch food. More in the French site. Great service cozy ambiance Semi formal setting with white table cloth.

Name: Natalie P.
Review: Amazing food and service was great. Would definitely come back again. The asparagus appetizer is a must try.

Name: Jason G.
Review: If you are staying in the Amsterdam city center, find Van Speyk. Had the Ribstuk with an amazing mushroom sauce and fresh mixed vegetables. Absolutely amazing. Staff was very friendly, the place is clean and a great design.

Name: Gold C.
Review: Great ambiance both inside and outside. Service was fantastic and the food was equally impressive. Love the croquettes and the portobello mushroom! One block from Renaissance hotel and close to city center.

Name: Tucker R.
Review: Delicious meal! Restaurant is gorgeous. We ordered the asparagus soup, the beef stew, the tuna, and the risotto, and everything was amazing.

Name: J P.
Review: Wow! What a pleasant surprise! Actually I should not be surprised based on the other reviews, however, this place far exceeded expectations for the food and service. Van Speyk salad and oysters are an tasty shared starter. My wife had the grilled chicken, and said it was perfectly prepared. I had the seafood risotto, and I'm familiar with the time & effort needed for preparing first class risotto. We shared the lemon pie with coconut ice cream for dessert. A unique, yet tasty combination. One thing that really sets this restaurant apart from many others is their customer service. Outstanding! We'll be back!

Name: Lauren C.
Review: I loved the cozy atmosphere of Van Speyk! It was perfect for date night. The food was amazing; the asparagus soup was so delicious. The main courses were unique and the perfect size. The wine was also amazing and the service was great as well. Definitely recommend!

Name: Teresa D.
Review: An amazing accidental find and Wow! Had:the duck confit, wonderful especially loved the polenta friesDutch sole really delicious and lightVegetarian dish with beluga lentils,truly fantastic.Service was top notched, attentive but not overly and really sweet. Can't say enough about this great night except make reservations, we were lucky and got in without them, and it was cold so we would rather have been in any ways.

Name: Sherlly O.
Review: Amazing dinner! Had the venison and oysters and it was delicious. By far best dinner i've had in Amsterdam. Make sure to reserve before.

Name: Leemor Y.
Review: Really great veggie breakfast with halumi, avocado, and eggs. A bit of a wait but they have a very organized process for the waitlist.

Name: Justin L.
Review: Organic. Free-range. Sustainable. B & R is a New Zealand/Brazilian-inspired cafe, serving various breakfast and lunch dishes. They take pride in partnering with local suppliers and making conscious efforts to focus on health and animal welfare. As a result, their prices are high, in an already expensive city. However, one can argue that these ethical decisions are priceless. And the food taste great, for what it's worth.The cafe is located in De Pijp, the neighborhood where our hotel was located. It's super close to the Museum Quarter and the original Heineken brewery, and the tram line that goes to Dam Square is nearby. We came for brunch, and there was a lot of people waiting. I got the Kiwi Brekkie, which I would say is a platter of all the best breakfast foods. You have a hot buttered toast, topped with two eggs ( I got poached), with bacon, sausage, tomato relish, spinach, and mushrooms on the side. Surprisingly it all went well together, I found everything super delicious and well proportioned. Great balance of meat and vegetables, and the eggs were poached nicely. Eggs Florentine had a lot of spinach, which is not as tasty in my opinion. Banana Nut Bread French Toast is a sweet option, topped with a strip of bacon. Portion sizes were decent for all dishes. Most of the eggs were € 12,00 to € 16,50. On the menu, they also have pancakes, waffles, salads, and other unique items. The drink choices are extensive, ranging from coffees to teas to milkshakes to juices to alcohol to New Zealand wine. Service was pleasant, we received our food pretty quickly. We also got glasses of water without asking, which was nice because other restaurants in Amsterdam make that super difficult. Maybe they sensed our Americanness.

Name: Gabriel N.
Review: Relatively but popular brunch spot! Great location to a lot of other things to see and do in Amsterdam. My friends and I came here before going to the Heineken Experience.They have a wide variety of options from your classic egg plates. bowls, salads, sandwiches and more. Of course, it aint brunch if they don't have some boozy drinks (which were quite tasty actually). I opted for the Navajo eggs which was pulled pork, avocado, mango salsa and chipotle cream on two eggs and toast. I gotta say, this was one of my favorite meals of my time in Amsterdam. The pork was super tender and flavorful. The mango salsa was honestly, the star of the plate. It was so nice and complemented the rest of the plate.All of my friends enjoyed their dishes. We would all recommend this place!!

Name: Lauren F.
Review: I came in for breakfast on a Friday morning and was seated after a very minimal wait. Even though it was probably not the thing to get, I ordered the Huevos Rancheros because it sounded the most appetizing at the moment. I was not disappointed. It was a simple combination of eggs, beans, avocado, tortilla and salsa, but I was satisfied. Paired with a matcha latte (for the wake up) and a salted caramel white Russian (for fun...it was Friday after all), I was quite happy with my breakfast at Bakers & Roasters.The design scheme was clean, breakfast place and it was busy but I felt like I got everything in time. Service was efficiently friendly and I paid with a chip card. I would come back to try the other coffee options. They appear to be coffee experts, so I'd check that out.

Name: Edward F.
Review: B&R Bakers and RoastersSmall and popular place for breakfast/brunch (though bigger than it looks). Broad selection that is dietary sensitive with vegan, gluten-free and dairy free options. They are not very flexible to substitutes as it interferes with the flow of orders but, if you must, they charge 2€ for the change.It all seems good. I had the Navajo eggs. The poached eggs were perfect, pulled pork just right and the mango salsa had a nice kick to it,

Name: Bonnie C.
Review: We were very hesitant to wait for a 2 person table over 50 minutes. But it was VERY worth it. The reservation process was very efficient and allowed us to move through the area and keep track of our place in line without sitting out front. The food was amazing. We travel quite a lot, all over the world, and try to eat breakfast out each day. This was in my top 5 breakfast spots I've ever tried. Pro-tip: it looked like the small bartop was open seating and did not get sat on the reservation list. They didnt mention that when we checked in for reservation, but be sure to ask if you're willing to sit there.

Name: Mehmet A.
Review: Great food, perfect for lunch. Would be eager to go soon again. Coffee is decent as well.

Name: Fay T.
Review: Nice and easy cafe next Heineken experience hall. Good for 1-2 for a brunch and cup of coffee.

Name: Cindy L.
Review: We decided to come here for breakfast after exploring the city all morning. The wait time was about 45 minutes and they put your cell phone number in and you get a link to check the status of your wait time.  I thought that was cool. We were able to order coffee, tea and drinks while we waited, so my husband got himself some coffee, me some hot tea and got my girls hot chocolate. Once we were seated, we decided on the B&R Special which had free range eggs fried or scrambled on top and it came with a side of mini pancakes. We also got the Eggs Royale, which is like eggs benedict with salmon in it. I love that they serve only free-range eggs here and they are trying to go for a healthy concept with their juices. I got a matcha green tea latte, it was delicious. My husband got the carrots turmeric juice and my kids loved it too. My kids got the kids breakfast to share, which came with mini pancakes, bacon and toast with eggs. We had a wonderful breakfast and our waitress was so sweet. It was one of my favorite meals in Amsterdam.

Name: Alexandria B.
Review: Bakers and roasters log T+15 minutes since I was seated at a stool at the counter. Time works differently here. The 5 minutes wait outside was actually 15 minutes according to my instruments.  I have now been on my stool for 17 minutes and it seems like some kind of phase shift is going on that makes me appear invisible to the people working here.  I can see them and the food looks and smells wonderful. If only I could find a way to break through so they can see me.  I have looked at the menu online and I have chosen my meal.  I will continue to keep this log until I am successful or I expire.T+24 minutes. I've had a breakthrough! For just a moment the barista came near enough to me so I could ask for coffee and a menu. Suddenly, I was no longer invisible. The hostess arm hugged me and confirmed that I am real not only in my own world but this one as well. I got and oat milk latte and I hope that in time to come, I shall receive a Benny with avocado. Until then...your faithful eater, Alex

Name: Chantel H.
Review: A very popular spot, down a cute alleyway near all the art museums. We picked this spot because it was so close to Rijksmuseum, it also near the Banksey museum and the Christmas market and ice skating rink. The wait wasn't too bad, we got in fairly quickly. I ordered the veggie brekkie, it was your standard eggs and potato breakfast but very good. Nothing I'd dream about but very good! Fair prices and delicious housemade kombucha.

Name: Maria E.
Review: *They close pretty early (4pm), FYI.Busy spot! We tried to get a table but the wait was over an hour. We put our name on the list and went to the Van Gogh museum. They called us while we were at the museum. We made it over there a little later but luckily they were still able to find us a table. This was on a Sunday by the way so it likely calms down during the week. Cute place with charming decor. Great menu options. I had the smoked salmon stack and it was really tasty. Friendly service. One complaint: the tables were a bit close together. I had someone directly behind me elbowing me.

Name: Emily W.
Review: Busy and bustling cafe but we got right in! It's a little noisy as all tables were filled but very nice energy. We started with a delicious matcha latte and orange juice. I enjoyed the Vege Brekkie - a flavorful sampling of veggies, eggs, halloumi cheese and toast. I would buy the chili jam by the bottle if I could! He enjoyed the Eggs Benny - perfectly cooked poached eggs atop bacon and toast topped with hollandaise. Everything was delicious and we left very full and satisfied. They are up front that the prices are not cheap but fair, quality ingredients are worth the price.

Name: Stephen Y.
Review: Breakfast was good, enjoyed the pancakes and service. Pancakes were light and fluffy with a pleasant surprise of blueberries in the middle. Ordered five stacks, and shared with my daughter. Neither of us finished the pancakes because we were full.

Name: Vincent L.
Review: A delightful cafe that's in between the Heineken Experience and the Museumplein and is within easy walking distance of both, Bakers & Roasters serves New Zealand and Brazil-inspired brunch and lunch fare in homage to the founders' roots. Everything I tried was quite delish and reasonably portioned given the quality and prices. Breakfast fare includes traditional items like eggs benedict and combination dishes of eggs, breakfast meats, veggies, and toast, while there's also an extensive menu of salads, sandwiches, bowls, baked goods. They also serve coffee and a good array of fresh juices. The atmosphere here is also lively, with a compact but reasonably bright interior and outdoor seats that are absolutely gorgeous in the warmer months. Thanks Yelpers for a great find!

Name: Keshia G.
Review: Such beautiful dishes and flavor to match. If you ca be sure to make a reservation in advance because they are always on wait. Luckily, they can text you when your table is ready. We tried a bunch of different things:Carrot Cake - Cute with good flavor, but not super fresh. My slice was also a little too cold for me especially since I ate it with my Chia Latte.Chia Latte - Yay! They have oat milk. But this Latte was my least favorite item. Idk just didn't really have much flavorHuevos Rancheros - No complaints! The dish is exactly what you'd expect from a huevos rancheros Salad Sampler - it was nice to find some fresh veggies in Amsterdam, but I wouldn't reorder this. Comes with 3 different salad. Beet, potatoes, and tomato. Mushroom Toast was unique and tasty. Toasted bread topped with marinated mushrooms.

Name: Marin J.
Review: Filling. Enough to almost share. I chose the special. Pricey but so filling you can easily skip lunch with no regrets. I asked for my eggs scrambled hard and they were perfect. Don't ignore the drink menu. Turmeric Apple ginger juice and orange juice were both winners. Tables inside tight and cosy. Seemed to be more relaxed seating in the garden area towards the back. Food was outstanding and menu delightful.

Name: Sergiu T.
Review: Definitely a recommended place to brunch in Amsterdam. And it has great vegetarian options. Service was neat.I loved:- Huevos Rancheros- Portobello ToastDidn't like:- The "3 Salad" dish (Besides the potatoes, the rest was kind of flavorless)Overall: Strong 4+

Name: Tiffany R.
Review: I really like this neighborhood so the restuarant already had a leg up. There is a lot to do in the area and its a convenient walk to the museums. At the same time it feels very much like a lived in neighborhood devoid of tourist traps. As for the menu. It was imaginative and fresh. Plenty of veggie options. They give you good service but don't pester you.

Name: Saige M.
Review: Everything about this place is yum!!! I highly recommend this place for brunch if you are in the area. The espresso is perfect, the service is great and the food tastes amazing. My only minus if a star is that it just felt a bit touristy, it seemed almost Americanized.

Name: Tung D.
Review: Very good ribs. I got here at around 4-5 PM, and it was empty. I sat at the bar and tried to order smoked ribs. The waiter was kind and gave me suggestion that if I ordered the princess dish, I would get to try both version of the ribs - the regular and the smoked ribs. I went with it and a coke. The served a generous portion of bread on the side.Anyways, onto the ribs. The regular ribs were falling off bones and very tender. Flavorful and a tiny bit sweet. The smoked ribs, on the other hand, were smokey and just a tiny bit on the salty side.It was great to compare the ribs side-by-side.The taste and seasonings were very different from American pork ribs.Great meal!

Name: John T.
Review: What most restaurants lack are sarcastic and blunt waiters. Look no further, cafe de klos has them! Please continue reading!Now that is all a good thing, rather what all BBQ joints need! The waiters make sure you get your ribs and beer when you are here. After all, you come here for ribs, if you don't order ribs why come! We loved the ribs and more importantly the funny waiters who made sure everything came out great with some humor.

Name: Dave S.
Review: First thing to note: Get reservations! This place is small and always busy. We wandered over just to gamble, and were told we'd have to wait 90 minutes. They have a sister bar across the street they send you to, and we went over to hang out. We checked back in 30 minutes and bar seats were open so we took them. Score!Great beer selection, with good wit biers and some solid Belgians. Good, lively bar, too, which is fun. The food is the thing, though! We got some escargot as an appetizer (it was good, but nothing too extraordinary), and then we ordered a massive 450g prime rib and the spare ribs. We were starving, but even then couldn't eat all this food! The spare rib was cooked perfectly, and was seasoned very well. Delicious steak. The ribs, though. Everyone here has said it, so I'm not telling you anything new. They are incredible. Seriously some of the best charcoal ribs I've had, and I have tried a lot. If you dig ribs, get them here and prepare to be blown away. They just fall off the bone, and are cooked so perfectly they just have to be tried.

Name: Eddie J.
Review: Located on Kerkstraat along the canal belt of Amsterdam, Cafe De Klos is a small gastro pub that specializes in smoked and barbecued meats. Be prepared for a long wait for a table. This establishment is small so I recommend sitting at the  full service bar if they can fit you in. Recommendations:Order the original spare ribs. The meat just falls off the bone. They also have Amstel on tap that goes great with the ribs.

Name: Tyra L.
Review: I was very skeptical when this rib place was recommended to me. I'm from the US and of course we think we're the best at stuff, but I really did think bbq was our thing. However, I do think these were some of the best ribs I've ever had. ( I'm from the Midwest so take it for what it's worth.) The rub or whatever they pup on them is just perfect. I was traveling solo for the day, but there were many other loners sitting inside at the bar with me. Pretty sure the bar is the only spot they let you have if you're alone so beware. It is also not air conditioned inside so it was a little warm on an 80+ degree day (Fahrenheit... to be clear) If you pay with credit card they charge you an extra 5%.

Name: Andy N.
Review: After traveling in Europe for about a week, I was missing some good ol' American fare like my ribs. Dutch food didn't necessarily fill me up all the way so a trip to Cafe De Klos really changed all of that.Like many other Yelpers have shared, this place has some BOMB ribs and was truly a great experience... if you're patient.The restaurant opens up around 16:00 in the afternoons and they get packed. Simply put, the bar/cafe that serves up these ribs is small so they typically send over any guests waiting to a local bar across the street. I'm sure they're both owned by the same person and that bar in particular had some of the friendly bartenders I ever interacted with in Europe. Definitely grab a beer or two.After waiting 45 minutes, one of the guys from the restaurant comes over and grabs you back into the bar area where you can finally order. My friend and I started off with their pate (€8,75) which was smooth and buttery. It came with unlimited bread (sooo American I know) and really helped quelled our hunger until our spare ribs (€21)  came out. Shortly after, the meat sensation came on a piping hot skillet and they were delicious. The meat was easy to pick off the bone and was really packed with flavor. Seriously, some of the best I've ever had.While the food is excellent, the wait did seem pretty long and the staff was just okay once we were seated. However, it's all worth it for the great ribs that they have here. Even if you're from the South and are unsure how these will live up to your expectations, give them a try. They will surely surprise you I guarantee that much.

Name: Karen S.
Review: Wow. I rarely go 5 stars, but this place is that good. The service was great. Super friendly and they all seem to enjoy being there. The food. I am probably in the minority for ordering the chicken, but it was delicious. Moist and flavorful - perfect! I really enjoyed the cole slaw/salad. A little tangy with kind of Italian dressing. Nice fresh crunchy side with all the decadent meat. The ribs were spot on. Husband liked both but the smoked had amazing flavor and char. Yum! We will definitely be back!

Name: Parker M.
Review: Nice spot near Leidseplein even though it's quite small. We had to wait nearly an hour for a table (no reservations) but they had us wait at the bar across and then got us when our table was ready. The spare ribs are fall off the bone delicious. For 22 euro, three racks of ribs with bread, salad, and sauces is a great deal for how filling and delicious it is. Some of the BEST ribs I ever had. The garlic sauce with the bread or ribs is soooooo good. Make sure to order the baked potato too, because it's massive and the garlic butter on it is unbelievable.

Name: Vy T.
Review: First off, the staff is witty and sarcastic, so if you cannot handle that, do not eat here. Period. Don't force yourself to like it otherwise you don't enjoy the food and be upset over the way they talk. Second, you need cash, otherwise it's a 15% service charge if you use plastic. There's an ATM across the street. Third, the portions are huge! So be prepared to togo or better yet, share with a friend while it's pipping hot and delicious. A sharing plate is an extra 7 euros FYI. Fourth, this is great BBQ but not worth more than a 30min wait imo. I heard wait times can be 2hrs+. Coming from the States, we have great BBQ also, so I'm likely slightly biased in this sense. Anyhow, so fortunately, we were able to be seated right away outside. We ordered the smoked ribs, a 24oz filet, and a baked potato. The food also comes with cole slaw and bread. As mentioned, the portions were huge! We wished we took this into account before ordering as we had a lot of leftover, our starving selves could not finish it all. Smoked ribs - amazing. The meat fell right off the bone and it wasn't too smoky at all. I got about 20 large bones, delicious. I was thankful for the bread to eat with it as it was a lot of meat. 24oz Filet - cooked to a perfect medium rare and also delicious. Cole slaw was good and helped cut the meat down as well. Overall good but again, I don't think it's worth waiting more than 30mins and please don't eat here if you are expecting that "American service". It doesn't exist here. They are witty and sarcastic.

Name: Ronald W.
Review: Given the other reviews here I ordered the mixed (grilled and smoked) ribs plate. It's huge! I'd suggest people split most of the entrees 2 ways and get some sides like the baked potato or soup I've seen mentioned. All entrees come with bread basket and salad (resembles cole slaw). The grilled ribs were pretty good like you would make at home but the smoked ribs have the consistency of a jerky. Given I made 2 meals out of this, it is a good bargain but I would have skipped the smoked ribs. As a comparison neither grilled or smoked are anyway as good as a typical Texas smoked beef rib... Way too lean.

Name: Andy N.
Review: This was the first meal I had in Amsterdam and it did not disappoint. The service was bleh but it fits the atmosphere. Grungy pub feel to the spot. We were quickly seated. The lamb shoulder here is the star. Even cooked at medium well it's a dish you will remember. The pate with bread was something I wanted more of. This is a meat lovers paradise with alcohol. If you're a meat and potatoes type of guy.. then Cafe De Klos is for you. I wanted to eat here again but it was super packed when I came back. It's also open pretty late compared to a lot of the other foodie spots in town. The ribs are also very popular here. There's two different kinds but one is much better than the other. Don't forget to order a french onion soup here.Recommendation: Lamb Shoulder , Ribs, pate , and french onion soup

Name: Mi N.
Review: Meat meat meat and more meat! We went here during our stay in Amsterdam because and the high reviews on Yelp as well as recommendations from friends and it was definitely a good place to check out if you're in Amsterdam.When we got there we were seated right away on the patio area. I think the restaurant itself was kind of small so if it gets busy, it'll probably take some time to wait for a table. Our waiter was very casual yet friendly and he showed us some popular items and warned us that we were getting a lot of food. Looking back, we should have just ordered one plate of meat and some sides because it was A LOT of food. The food itself was amazing! I got ribs that were half smoked half regular and it was so juicy and tender. My boyfriend got lamb which was also really good, though I'm not a fan of lamb in general. Tips: 1. If you're going in a party of 2, just get 1 order of meat (ribs are recommended) and order some sides lol2. Skip this place if you're a vegetarian.

Name: neil m.
Review: Pro: Very good cocktails, great atmosphere, reasonable price. Con: the menu is a hard piece of plastic that is cumbersome to use/open, our first server was a space cadet (didn't know drinks, ingredients, etc) but second person was amazing.

Name: James M.
Review: Pretty pricey butAmazing meat qualityHuge portions so order one portion first for 2 people and see if you are still hungryBaked potato probably freshest best taste ever too ...by american standards

Name: Mike C.
Review: Warning:  expect a 45 min - 1 hour wait.  Doesn't matter what time you show up.  Rest assured:  the wait is with it.  Tip:  If you check in with the staff - you can tell him you will wait across the street at their bar and have drinks.  He will come get you when your table/ or bar seat is ready.  The food is great. I had three in my party and we are typical Americans that over eat.  We ordered a mixed rib plat as an appetizer and each order the small Sirloin.  No sides- and that was more than enough food.  Damn near too much.  The monk beer is great but at 7%+ alcohol it will leave you on your ass after 4 pints so be careful.  You will find any number of steak houses without a wait.  At least a dozen in walking distance but there is a reason for that. I tried one and it was subpar.   Try this place.  You will be glad you did.

Name: Isabel S.
Review: Stumbled across this restaurant online, decided to give it a try on our first night in Amsterdam. The place was full, we were seated pretty quickly, friendly staff, and decent amount of choices to accompany the ambiance. My meal was cooked perfectly, very tender and juicy. I chose the sweet vanilla corn as my side- a win for the night- delicious. And the wine paring suggested as very tasty, typically stick to one glass of wine (not much of a drinker), I had two glasses. I would definitely be interested in going back when/if I am ever in Amsterdam again.

Name: Karla T.
Review: Walked in without reservations and luckily there was one available table left. Staff was very friendly. We ordered the wings, sweet potato fries, cannibale Royale Burger, a beer and long island. Everything tasted really good and the portions were a good size. Also the decorations here are pretty cool if you are into serial killer movies.

Name: Teryl R.
Review: Ran into this spot because the original spot was closed. First I would like to say that I appreciate the waitress for seating us without reservations (didn't know we needed because of last minute changes). We were seated quickly, and spaced out from other guests. I love how multiple people check with us to see if we needed anything at our table, great customer service. The food was just what we needed and the prices were reasonable. If I ever come back to Amsterdam I will make sure to stop by again.

Name: Elle F.
Review: Looking for late night food wasn't too bad in Amsterdam . I loved how this place is open until 3 am. We got to the restaurant around 1 am and there was a lot of people. I loved the vibes in there . A fun place to have dinner & drinks.They have a late night menu which Consist of items with an owl next to it. We got the ribs , classic burger , wAtermelon feta salad, and fries . All the food was delicious . Hands down the burger was amazing. It was soo good with the watermelon salad. Paired nicely. Also , hands up for the guy at the bar who made my margarita. It was perfect. I was amazed by how good it was I ordered another!Huyen our waitress was super helpful and attentive. We were asking her where to go out and I loved how she gave us selections ( although she really doesn't go out ) I thought that was sweet of her. She gave great service .I love that this place serves qualityFood for late night hours. Very impressed and went a second time during our period in Amsterdam!

Name: Brian M.
Review: 2 X Cannibale Royale Ales2 X Sauvignon Blancs1 X Rib Slab1 X Pulled Pork Sandwich1 X Friets = $47,20.= Delicious across the board, great service, fast wifi.Tip:  Not a ton to look at, but the table for two window side offered a bit more light and was a nice spot for looking outside.

Name: Jacques I.
Review: We visited Cannibale Royale, as it was listed as a Yelp Elite pick for Amsterdam.  After visiting I now know why.  Cannibale Royale is a chill, hip restaurant with good eats and solid drinks. We sat at the bar, as one of the employees mentioned that all of the tables were for dinner service.  We only wanted some bites and mostly drinks, so found three stools at the bar, which ended up being the best seats in the house.  It's where all the magic happens. The bartender became our friend.  We saw that they served Stone Brewery beers here, which has awesome IPAs, so started with beers.  For a cocktail I ordered a Manhattan, and as the menu details, it's slowly-stirred.  I witnessed the bartender slowly stir it and the poor gal had to do it twice for me, since I had another.  I still think it's odd that Manhattans served in Amsterdam are with ice (and sometimes sugar); and although it was served in ice, this Manhattan was way better than the other Manhattans I ordered while in Amsterdam.  Thank goodness. Food was yummy!  One of my friends had the bitterballen and my other friend had the roasted veggies, while I ordered the nachos with chicken.  Everything was super tasty.  The nachos were good, especially with the chicken, which I recommend adding.  There was a good spice to the chicken.  It was also a good size for sharing.Cannibale Royale was a fun place to visit for drinks, and I'm glad we stayed long enough for some bar bites.  During the two hours we were there we witnessed that every table was filled.  There was even a line at the door, waiting for bar seats to open up.  It was quickly snatched as soon as we got up to depart.  Cannibale Royale is a popular spot and worth checking out if you're in town.

Name: Marian M.
Review: It was really late at night, we just arrived to Amsterdam from Bergen. There were not many options but as foodies, dinner its a big deal for us. Cannibale Royale is a trendy-rock bar with very tasty bitterbals, burgers and great beer.Era muy tarde a la noche, recién llegabamos de Brujas a Amsterdam. No había muchas opciones pero como foodies, la cena es un tema para nosotros. Cannibale Royale es un bar trendy-rockero con muy sabrosas "bitterbals", hamburguesas y gran selección de cervezas.

Name: Harol L.
Review: Good ribs and good service! A super busy restaurant in the red light district. Overall a good experience, I would recommend this place for somegood barbecue ribs.

Name: Jodi G.
Review: Desperately searching for a kitchen open late, we found this place. It was a fun, funky little place, with good food and strong drinks. I have to admit- it was pretty amusing to be in Amsterdam, enjoying nachos and margaritas, in a cannibal themed bar, listening to 50 cent bumping loudly! What a combo!

Name: Shoba P.
Review: Delicious food. Enjoyed dinner at a shared table and met new people. We got the pulled pork burger and the impossible burger and they were HUGE and extremely fulfilling. I also had grilled broccoli was delicious.  I would have given 5 stars but our waitress was not very friendly, she brought out the wrong wine and I requested a beer which she never brought. We were there to have a good time and I did not have the energy to get annoyed so went with the flow. Reservations a plus but not needed.

Name: Amanda G.
Review: Highly recommend, but reserve at least a week ahead! We were in Amsterdam for my husband's birthday, and I'd read many rave reviews about this place. I forgot to book a reservation, and when we arrived it was fully booked on a Monday night. The host said we could wait for a table at the bar (there are 6 seats there), so we gave it a chance. Fortunately, we waited only about 20 minutes. Service/Atmosphere: The bartender and staff were friendly and seem to enjoy being there. Atmosphere is interesting... antique photos on the walls and baby dolls hanging from the ceiling. Great playlist and the music wasn't too loud.Food: Amazing! I had the flat iron steak and sweet potato fries; he had the ribs and regular fries. Everything came out hot and delicious. The ribs were especially good, with lots of flavor and not too saucy. Will return next time we're in town.

Name: Alaysia P.
Review: Food was amazing, especially the lamb chops and wings. It's really busy in the evenings, so it took a while to get service.

Name: Telmo O.
Review: I tried vegetarian food, paleo diet, soy-milk, even shrimp (they're the cockroaches of the sea), so I am not one to reject a new experience.When I was invited to this place, I prepared as best I could - saw the original Hannibal trilogy and a few vampire movies (closest thing to a royal cannibal I guess).The staff was really helpful even though we had no reservation. Once we got our seat, one of the best parts of the restaurant came to light -- the menu!They give really funny names to their dishes, so I ended up having the "Le Modest" while my gf had "Le Magnifique". I guess we were both thinking about each other when we ordered, although she's too modest to admit it.Small note for the menu item "L'Absurde" -- a 1000g steak, that few lived to tell the tale. There is even a hall of fame for them, right by the entrance, with a board of who ate this beast and how many times they did it! I could already see we were in for a treat when the cutlery was placed at our sides. A strong, purposeful fork paired with what I'm gonna call a "murder" knife. Didn't know how much meat was coming round the corner but whatever it was coming our way, we were definitely ready to hack & slash our way through it.Then, the meat! Wow, I don't know who that person was, but it was delicious (probably a former cross fitter). The meat portion is huge and I liked the fact that it was served on a small meat carving board, to really let you feel like a butcher. Meat lovers will rejoice of course, while vegans might reconsider some annoying life choices they made.As for the space, it's this cool dark environment, not very noisy, where you can have a normal conversation or seat as a group without disturbing others too much. There are these cannibal references all over the walls which make this place really fun and unique. Dare to enter if you're around the area ;)Bonus point: open till late (1 or 2 am I think). Hard to find places like this in Amsterdam.

Name: Daniel F.
Review: Pretty good burger and meat for Europe in an American style joint. The fries are good. Overall a solid experience. It wasn't the best but bang for buck it's pretty good.

Name: Gary H.
Review: The name De Foodhallen says it all. A big, awesome food hall. It's a bit overwhelming when first entering. Restaurant booths cover both sides to the very back until you reach a seperate restaurant "Kanarie Club".  It's not the cheapest, but it is an event. Great for large groups if you get there early.I am sure most of the food places here are absolutely most delicious. I know Fento is good. There are bars in the center. It's just a bit busy for me with the crowds and you cannot reserve seating. It was really nice when you could sit at a table and order from your phone from anywhere (during the 2020, 2021 times). It's definitely a landmark and a must to visit. Not touristy but also great for tourists.

Name: Lynne C.
Review: Fun food court with a great assortment of options and restaurants to choose from! Fried chicken, Banh Mi's, burgers, the list goes on and on! Filled with tourists and locals alike, I would highly recommend finding a place first and then getting your food. When I came it was absolutely packed and since I was alone, ended up just eating my sushi standing. The sushi was surprisingly dry and not that great but the food hall itself had a really great atmosphere and super fun vibe!

Name: Marin J.
Review: Super cool spot with good variety! Bulls and dogs was decent but not as amazing as I'd hoped. The meatball was good but overpriced. Wings were ok. Too much to try, we need to go back!

Name: Jacques I.
Review: I love that Amsterdam has a food hall, a concept I'm a fan of.  Why settle on one food destination when you can select from a variety?My friends and I came here to check it out and were pleased with what we found.  The place was packed on a weekday during the dinner hour, which is always a good sign.  Like a typical food hall, there are various eateries throughout the floor with lots of seating usually in the center and a few bars with counter seating.  I advise pulling up a seat at one of the bars for the easy access to booze.  Of the eateries, it's a pretty good variety, from a Dutch specialty of bitterballen, to Asian eats like dim sum and baos, to BBQ and wood-oven pizza.  Lots to choose from, so go with friends and share.  All of the vendors accept card.  Glad to have visited De Foodhallen, as it's a popular place for locals and tourists.  Throughout my entire time in Amsterdam I met most Americans here at the food hall!  It's a fun place to socialize, drink and eat.

Name: Ryan A.
Review: If you know me by now, I tend to make frequent stops at food halls, or indoor/outdoor markets as I find them to less touristy and more geared to locals (In most cases).De Foodhallen flirted with a tourist trap, but ultimately brought a locals vibe more than anything. It is the perfect place if going out with a bunch of friends who are very picky in terms of what they prefer to eat. It is littered with food stalls serving tasty meals from around the globe. Want ramen...they got it, want tacos...they got it, want hamburgers...they got it, want local bitterballens...I think you get the idea. Being a foodie, I was in heaven, I must of done four to five rounds before deciding on what I wanted. Being day six in the Netherlands and not having much local food, specifically the fried balls of goodness otherwise known as Bitterballen, I had to cave! They offer a platter with all different flavors at one of the stalls for a great price point. My travel partner decided she wanted a burger, a blue cheese to be specific. Both meals were phenomal, might I say one of the better while staying in Amsterdam. I will forewarn you, this place is popular, so much that seating can be a pain in the arse. If you have a friend(s) with you, it may be wise to split up with some finding seating depending how busy it is. Either way, make sure to bookmark this wonderful food hall, not only for their scrumptious food, but also their beer stalls and awesome lounge areas!

Name: Sherry H.
Review: Super cool spot with good variety! Bulls and dogs was decent but not as amazing as I'd hoped. The meatball was good but overpriced. Wings were ok. Too much to try, we need to go back!

Name: Brianne S.
Review: If you're in Amsterdam and love food this is definitely not a place to miss! Easy to reach by tram (just Google directions) this housed about 20 different food/drink vendors all under one roof. In a mood for Vietnamese? No problem. In a mood for Dim Sum? They got you! In a mood for a both and a side of tacos? This is your place! Seating here is definitely hard to come by but you'll find a spot or somewhere to stand and eat your food. You're going to keep on the move to get different things anyway. There is a great beer bar here with cans/bottles/drafts from all around the world, and an excellent gin & tonic bar across the way serving up real classy drinks to go along with anything you chose from the food hall. We were only in A'dam for a few days but I loved this place so much we came back twice to try even more! If ever we find ourselves back in town, this will most definitely be on the list to visit again!

Name: Tim X.
Review: It was around the corner from our AirBnB on Ten Katenstraat, and there's plenty of choices. We tried the Vietnamese place (Viet View), supposedly "Street Food" but it wasn't quite what we expected - the bowls were a little too salted with soy and there was no soup. The Banh Mi was decent and filling, good choice.The standout was Jabugo, where they had Jamon Iberico de Bellotta and some really good manchego, both of excellent quality, albeit quite pricey.A great place to eat if you are around the area.

Name: Cathy Z.
Review: Neat concept in Amsterdam a bit off the tourist block. This place seemed to have something for everyone! We shared a burrata board and some tacos. The tacos were honestly incredible. They were pulled chicken and had pickled onion on them. So good I should have ordered a platter! The burrata was nice too. They top it with some truffle oil. Not the best burrata I have but a tasty snack during the day.

Name: Valerie C.
Review: Fun place to go sample many items. I enjoyed the Amsterdam meat hush puppies the best. De Allen I think it was called! The sampler was great with their  special mustard.

Name: Pia M.
Review: 5 stars for Gin & Tonic bar.5 stars for the stand with the 5-cheese hot dog.5 stars for their great selection of beer.4 stars for the stand with the Jamon Iberico platters.There are lots of different vendors here like dim sum, sushi, seafood, burgers, tacos, tapas etc.  Although Yelp says they open until 1am, most stalls close between 10-11pm.  Also most of the stalls do not take cash, so make sure to bring a credit/debit card.Enjoy!!

Name: Deana M.
Review: Great food and good vibes. Can be hard to get a seat. We were lucky there were only two of us and enjoy sitting at bar tops. Some places are card only FYI. We enjoyed getting bites from different venues and listening to the DJ.

Name: Cicely T.
Review: Pretty cool food hall right next to our hotel.Got the meat and cheese place and de ballen bar 'bitterballen' flight. The bitterballens were amazing! You must try!! I will be dreaming about these things in the future. There was a beer bar too which served beer from around the world. Keep in mind, the foodhall is open at 11am but most places aren't open until Noon or later. I went to De Ballen Bar at 12 and the lady there said she wouldn't be open for another 30 mins!

Name: Anna I.
Review: Foodhallen should be considered a tourist attraction in Amsterdam because it's literally amazing. It's basically a hall which different food vendors similar to a market. The food options are absolutely amazing. The hall, itself, is beautiful and the bathrooms are very clean. They have a lot of tables but it does get crowded. You'd be surprised how packed it could get. My partner and I shared a chicken pita wrap and ordered a burger from the Butcher. The burger was literally life changing. It was one of the most delicious, perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned and freshest burgers I've ever had. My grammar is all over the place, but I think you get the point. The Butcher is definitely worth the long line and wait. I think anyone can find a good place at this Food Hall. If you're a vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian or a meat eater.

Name: Nicole M.
Review: It is SO hot in here! Super stuffy - they need some fans or some air circulation going through this place.That aside though, it's a pretty cool spot. Lots of different eateries to choose from so there's something for everyone. First time trying bitterballen and that was fun with all the different flavors. The pizza from Renatos was delicious with lots of prosciutto in it. The hummus plate from Maza was pretty good but the tacos from Taqueria Lima were only okay.  And then there were places that, coming from SF, I'd never get something from - €5 for 3 pieces of dim sum from Dim Sum Thing is outrageous. But then again if I hadn't had dim sum in a while, who knows what money I'd pay for a fix.We came on a Friday night so it was understandably crowded, and it took over half an hour to finally get a full table for our party of 7. Good spot though for people to kick back with friends after work.

Name: Penelope M.
Review: We have no reservation,  but I made sure we went near opening time.  Moeders is so popular,  they're fully booked for the rest of April. Thankfully, we were seated as soon as we came in,  provided we can free up the table in an hour and a half.  Speed eating is my forte, so this was not a problem.  We took the Dutch Rice dishes. Ironically, rice wasn't part of it. A sampler of different Dutch dishes to try. I detected some tourists here, or maybe just local fellow yelpers. Or maybe, they were tourist yelpers, lol. To start, they served warm bread, with a mayonnaise and relish on the side. Then the two main dishes came in their cute little pots. There were potatoes cooked three ways: boiled, roasted(that was the best!), and mashed. The sausage was marvelous, so was the bacon.  I haven't seen them served crispy,  but they were lean. We finished our meal ahead of schedule,  and would have tried dessert,  but my belly was bursting at the seams.  Actually, it's always bursting at the seams.  The vibe of this place was quite reminiscent of Monell's in Nashville. Staff was all hardworking, happy people.  I hope they really are,  because they make my tummy happy.

Name: Sharon T.
Review: Moeders isn't exactly a hidden gem, but a beloved establishment and the epitome of strong women empowerment that is very much embraced today.Open its front door and you'll catch a small preview of the inside: the walls and ceiling filled to the brim with photos in pretty frames as a tribute to mothers and hard-working Dutch women, and not an inch of space left to spare for an extra 4x6. Remove the novelty photos, the neon pink lights will probably have me mistaken it for a retro American diner."Moeders" is exactly what it sounds like: Dutch for "mothers". The food is made with love from the force behind the restaurant: Annie, Betty, and Corrie, each with their own respective speciality menu of traditional Dutch food. I came here to try Annie's Stamppot, which is mashed potatoes mixed with sauerkraut, topped with bacon, meatball, a smoked sausage link from one of Amsterdam's best butchers, Butcher Louman, and a side of gravy to shower your Stamppot in. I admit that I hadn't had a proper breakfast and lunch that day and had a light meal only 20 minutes prior to arriving here but I made sure I finished everything on my plate. It was also my first time trying Stamppot and I LOVED it. It felt as if I was sitting in someone's home and indulging in all the love and care they put in. I love mashed potatoes, so this was great for me. Not sure if the gravy pairing actually did much, other than make it more moist, but the meat toppings were fresh and delicious. If you're not a fan of sauerkraut, you may be disappointed, which is a shame since Stamppot is a hearty meal itself. I suggest coming here before peak hours for an early dinner since it seems like they're jam-packed with reservations, but totally accommodating if you eat before the rush sweeps in.

Name: Ali Can C.
Review: What a heartwarming concept; but you should know the decor is not the only good thing about this place. The food is really really delicious; we tried the Dutch sampler plates and it was enough for two people. The service is very friendly and welcoming. They were so kind to accept our mothers' pictures to display as well.We will come back again next time when we are in Amsterdam!

Name: Erik S.
Review: On our first day in Amsterdam we found this place and based on good yelp reviews we decided to try it. We were early enough to get a table without reservation, many people were turned away after that because apparently they were booked out for the weekend.Very friendly service. Very "home cooked meal" vibe.We had the rice dish which was a sampling of all of the Dutch delicacies (2 meat pots, boiled potatoes, little baked potatoes, and mashed potatoes with a slab of bacon and a sausage...which was basically a "girthy hotdog", there was also some cabbage and apple sauce)The experience was good and we left full. Don't expect fine dining or anything trendy because it isn't. But it was friendly, tasty, and definitely was a good way to start the trip.

Name: Alice C.
Review: When in the place, always give the traditional food a try. In Amsterdam, Moeders has made their name as one of the city's top places to go for traditional Dutch home cooked style cuisine.Stepping into the small restaurant, where tables are set cozily together (but not so close as to making it hard to have a good conversation), the place is laid out like a cozy old school mothers dining room. The walls are covered with photos of "moms" from all over the world it seems.They offer a la carte or 3 course special sets where prices change depending on your choice of entree. They start you off with a lovely basket of fresh crusty bread, I literally could hear the crunch of the crust as they cut it! For the appetizers we went for the appetizer sampler and the island egg dish. The sampler offers a lovely variety, while the egg dish was amazing with a sweet potato "shell" and filled with spinach, onion and cheese and topped with an egg. For the entree, we both went with hotchpotch, me the meat one with sauerkraut stampot and him the vegetable one. They were both delicious and very filling with all that potato. I thought I did a good job but felt like I barely made much of a dent - doggie bag it is! Last but most definitely not least, apple pie for dessert was absolutely amazing. The apples were coated lightly in cinnamon and not too sweet, making each bite with the accompanying whipped cream and ice cream truly delicious. A great finale to a delish dinner. And to digest all this, we made sure to walk all the way back home!

Name: Alison R.
Review: My husband and I happened to stumble upon this restaurant during our latest trip and were happy to experience what is considered true Dutch food.I ordered some lamb skewers, which were very well seasoned and very tender but were much more pink that I'm used to eating lamb so that was kind of a turn-off. I'm sure it was fine and it was probably my fault for not understanding how lamb can be prepared, but regardless too pink for me. Hubby had another traditional dish and was very happy with his choice. The ambiance is really incredible with all of the pictures of the mom's on the walls, makes the atmosphere really home-y and unique. Would recommend!

Name: Matthew L.
Review: Made reservations about a month in advance for a group of 8 on a Saturday at 6pm, it's not the largest restaurant, so you're going to want to make reservations, especially for a larger group.I'm all about eating traditional food during trips, so I knew this was a must. I didn't really know much about Dutch food aside from herring and fries, so coming to Moeders was a great learning experience. Our group got a few of the full meals that are for a minimum of two at 20.50 Euros a person, which came with a couple of the stews, potato salad w/ sausage and bacon, fried or baked potatoes, apple sauce, and all the love from mama, because this restaurant has pictures of mothers all over the place, with the menu matching this theme. There are menu items from different mothers apparently. We also got a couple of orders of the market fish (turned out to be salmon), and a couple of orders of the spare ribs. The beef stews and the spare ribs really stood out, with so much flavor and heartiness. The spare ribs actually tasted like a mix between an Asian and European rib, so it was really unique. The beef in the stews melted in my mouth, with one being a lighter, more brothy sauce with a more tender cut of meat, and the other in a thicker sauce with a bit more chew in the cut of beef. Both were good in their own ways, but I think the consensus was we all preferred the thicker beef stew. If this is what traditional Dutch food is like, it wouldn't exactly be my favorite, but I can still totally get behind it!

Name: Margaret L.
Review: This is your traditional Dutch food. So I originally wanted to go to a different restaurant nearby but that one was just unpromising. Everytime we came they kept telling us to come by so I decided to try Moeders because I saw good things on tripadvisor/yelp.We came here for traditional Dutch food because we haven't had a chance to experience Dutch food in Amsterdam! The service here is good, everyone's real nice. If you don't make reservations, they do their best to seat you immediately. I felt very fortunate we were able to get seated quickly.After reviewing the menu, we decided to do the dutch meal with the pot roast and different sides. When the food came out, it was delicious. I like everything. The red cabbage, roasted potatoes, boiled potatoes, apple sauce accompanied the roasts well. Although I wouldn't say it was anything special but the food reminds me of home cooked food.The decor is also unique - mismatching utensils and plates and lots of photos of mother everywhere. When we were here, there was a large party (more than 10) seated and they also seemed very content with everything. This is definitely a family restaurant. If you want Dutch food in Amsterdam, come here!

Name: Sol C.
Review: Moeders has a fun vibe (see the many photos posted to yelp of their walls covered in framed pictures), great beer selection, decent service and excellent food. Plus, when in Amsterdam we wanted to at least try some traditional Dutch food. Dutch food, it seems, is similar to German or even Irish with lots of meats and sausages and potatoes.The portions at Moeders were large (which we gathered from eyeing our neighbors at dinner) and therefore we skipped appetizers and went straight for entrees. I am a lover of all things fermented so I could not pass up the sauerkraut stampot. This was a hearty portion of sauerkraut mixed with mashed potatoes, topped with gravy and served with a sausage, a meatball and bacon. It was fantastic and the potato was loaded with sauerkraut - so if you are really looking for your average mashed potato, this will be disappointing. But, if you freakishly love sour cabbage, like me, you will be thrilled.The other entree we tried was also excellent and was a meat stew served in an adorable red pot with potatoes and red cabbage. The meat was perfectly tender and the stew broth was excellent and full of flavor. Save the bread they bring to the table to dip in this stew! On the side, the apple compote was a nice addition to the entrees.For dessert, do not miss the apple pie. This is actually more of a moist, delicious slice of buttery cake filled with cooked apples and raisins served with ice cream and whipped cream. I would eat a slice of this every day if I could!Tip: we made a reservation online a few weeks in advance and I'm glad we did as it was quite busy.

Name: Rich S.
Review: Great place to eat for typical Dutch fare. Mommas home cooking best describes this place. Interesting decor but extremely long stated wait times. Staff could be rude if you don't have a reservation but be diligent and hold fast, you will get off that wait list. Try the Dutch special and the apple pie for desert. This ain't your ordinary apple pie!!!  The Dutch platter with its mix of beef stew, mash potatoes, apple sauce, bacon and sausage is delish!!!

Name: Brendan E.
Review: The Restaurant: a cozy, always busy, no frills restaurant serving up mom's Dutch home cooking. My mom doesn't cook, so this gave me a nice glimpse of what coulda been!Ordered: the spareribs and the hodge podge.Hodge Podge: a hodge podge of traditional dutch food. A minimum of two ppl must order it. Comes with two different kinds of beef stews, an assortment of slaws, assortment of potatoes, and sauces. I threw everything on my plate and mixed them up, just like when I was a kid. Everything was delicious - quite the hearty meal.Spareribs - a nice rack of ribs. Tender/fall off the bone. You can choose which kind of sauce you want - bbq, hot and spicy, etc. I went with bbq and they were delicious. Pro-tip: this place is often full, so book a reservation ahead of time, especially when the weather gets cold and ppl can't eat in the outside seating. If the outdoor seating is available, you can usually show up without a reservation and wait anywhere between 30-60 mins for a table.

Name: Athena C.
Review: We came here for Sunday lunch luckily without any reservation and were able to get a table quickly without wait. I didn't realize Moeders means Mothers in Dutch and was surprised to see pictures of mothers everywhere on the wall. It does give me a warm fuzzy feeling about this diner. I heard traditional Dutch food is hard to find nowadays and this is one of the few good ones in Amsterdam. I ordered the Hotchpotch and my husband and father-in-law shared the classic Dutch Rice Dish. There was so much food! My dish comes with spinach meshed potato although you can choose either spinach or sourkraut as well as a giant sausage, huge meatball and bacon. I could barely finish this and shared it with my son. My hubby's dish is even bigger so two people to share are definitely adequate. It also comes with meshed potato, apple sauce, sausage, beef stew, beef stew with onion, bacon, gravy and red cabbage. The stews were amazing and the beef was so tender and juicy!It was a great experience for my family and I would come again and prepared to be stuffed!

Name: Sylvia B.
Review: A friend who lives nearby this spot told me this place is almost never available for walk-ins so when a reservation spot popped up recently we grabbed it.  Very much your homey Dutch comfort food.  It's called "mothers" and no surprise the place is almost covered floor to ceiling with pictures of mothers and the menu is divided into the dishes of the three mothers that are currently cooking there.  You can't miss with the classic stamppot - very filling - but save room for the made-in-house speculoos ice cream, which has a semi-freddo like texture.  Priced somewhere between reasonable and expensive.

Name: Kally C.
Review: Regarding Gluten-Free...1) Menu with very clearly marked items denoting gluten-free2) Many options3) The BEST gluten-free bread I've ever had after eating GF for 10+ years!  That's not hyperboyle.  The GF bread is f'ing legit!The food was very good and the meal lasted for quite a while.  Plan on making an event out of this

Name: Jenny P.
Review: Found this gem online. Wasn't sure what to expect but all the reviews recommended the ribs and the hodgepodge. Unfortunately the wife wasn't feeling to well so we were not able to eat at the restaurant so I went alone ordered a few items to go. The wife was a big fan of the stew which came as a recommendation from the staff and she could not have been happier. The spare ribs were also exceptional. Everyone there was very welcoming and the food was great too. Would recommend this place to anyone and everyone visiting Amsterdam!

Name: Amber R.
Review: Great place to get a traditional Dutch meal! Love the vibe and staff there. If it's your first time having Dutch food, it might be a good idea to get the family-style dinner because it includes a small portion of everything. Make sure you order the beers there too!

Name: Ron L.
Review: Watch out...heed their warning.  Wear your asbestos suit.It's spicy hot, they warned us. Not being the same person I was years ago, I did heed their warning, but my dinner companion wanted to be the macho one and tried to brave it.He failed.  I enjoyed the rest of my dinner.

Name: Craig G.
Review: For the last meal of my trip, I had to satisfy my craving for Indonesian. Sampurna is a sleek, cozy spot not far from the flower market in the city center.
