Reservations are recommend, as this place will fill up pretty quick, though I got there early enough to snag a table without a wait. As soon as you're seated, you're greeted with a bowl of rice crackers and three sambals (sauces, not unlike an Indian chutney). The menu features a number of satay skewers, a selection of rice dishes, and a few rijstafel (rice table: small portions of several dishes for a table to share). Dining solo, a rijstafel was out of the question, but the ayam penggang seten caught my eye.I'm pretty sure the literal translation of the dish is "fried chicken in Satan sauce", which seemed apt: this was one of the most brutally spicy dishes I've ever eaten. Aside from the intense heat, the dish was actually very flavourful, with garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and other spices shining through. Every entree here comes with a number of small side dishes: white rice, pickled veggies, veggies in a coconut curry sauce, and fried tempeh. Everything was delicious, all the better when washed down with a glass of Bintang (an Indonesian beer).The staff was friendly, but harried.

Name: Gurpreet L.
Review: While Yelping places to grab a late dinner, we stumbled across Sampurna which was perfect for us because we had wanted to try Indonesian food in Amsterdam. We got here around 9:50 PM on a Thursday night and were told that kitchen was about to close (the restaurant closes at 11 PM but we learned that the kitchen closes at 10). We were quickly seated and scanned our options as quickly as possible so that we could get our order in. There were multiple vegetarian options for me to choose from which was a delightful surprise.I ended up picking the Tahu Bumbu Bali, a tofu dish, while my friend with what looked like a kebab plate. Our food was scrumptious! The tofu was perfectly crispy on the outside and it was smothered in this spicy sauce that had a perfect amount of kick. Although I was unable to try my friend's dish, from the way they were scarfing it down, I think they enjoyed their food. In a town with tons of Indonesian options, I highly recommend this place!

Name: Jacques I.
Review: Ya gotta have Indonesian food in Amsterdam! My friends and I came here for dinner, as we read that Sampurna was one of the best spots for Indonesian food.  Plus, while we were at the flower market, we saw that it was just right across from it, so already knew where to find it!I am unfamiliar with Indonesian food, but after having had it at Sampurna, I want to learn and EAT more!  We came here without a reservation and fortunately, was able to get seated for the three of us on a weeknight.  The space isn't large, as the dining room is split into two rooms and is on the more narrow side.  The menus are in both Dutch and English and there's a full bar here.Not knowing anything about Indonesian food, I asked the server what she recommended for someone's first time having it.  She recommended the Sate Solo Menu if we all wanted to get something different and not share.  The sate solo menu is a great option for someone who wants to try multiple items, but doesn't have anyone to share it with.  One of my friends is vegan, so couldn't share any of the meat items and my other friend wanted a different kind of entree.  Therefore, the sate solo menu was for me.  Before we ordered our main entree, we were provided complimentary chips.The sate solo menu came with Indonesian fried rice, two chicken skewers, two beef skewers, two goat skewers, spicy chicken in a coconut sauce, steamed veggies in a peanut sauce, mango salad, boiled egg in a spicy sauce, beans with bamboo shoots, cucumber salad and coconut with peanuts.  Doesn't that sounds amazzzzzing?  Well, it was!  It's spendy at nearly 30 bucks, but I think it's worth trying if you want to have a little bit of everything.  Gosh, what did I love the most?  Everything was so tasty and went together very well, with a little bit of sweet, a little bit of sour, a little bit of spice and a little bit of creamy.  It's truly the best of all worlds.  Of the skewers I liked the goat one the best, as the meat was very tender and flavorful with however it was seasoned.  But all of the skewers had a slight grill taste, which added a nice lightness to all the other plates with sauces.  The spicy chicken in a coconut sauce was incredible, as the coconut flavor really came out with spice, which is just how I like curries.  The steamed veggies in a peanut sauce were crispy and light, and would've even liked them without the peanut sauce.  Though, the peanut sauce adds a nice flavor, especially when eaten with a skewer and the fried rice.  Mango salad was refreshing, with a nice, chill to it and added sweetness to the palate.  Again, all the different taste buds really came through with the solo sate menu.  I left full and happy. Indonesian food, I need to eat you again!  We all loved our food and Sampurna was definitely one of the best meals I had while in Amsterdam.  I loved the various flavors, complementing one another in my meal.  I highly recommend the sate solo menu if you don't do family style here.

Name: Ron L.
Review: Watch out...heed their warning.  Wear your asbestos suit.It's spicy hot, they warned us. Not being the same person I was years ago, I did heed their warning, but my dinner companion wanted to be the macho one and tried to brave it.He failed.  I enjoyed the rest of my dinner.

Name: Craig G.
Review: For the last meal of my trip, I had to satisfy my craving for Indonesian. Sampurna is a sleek, cozy spot not far from the flower market in the city center. Reservations are recommend, as this place will fill up pretty quick, though I got there early enough to snag a table without a wait. As soon as you're seated, you're greeted with a bowl of rice crackers and three sambals (sauces, not unlike an Indian chutney). The menu features a number of satay skewers, a selection of rice dishes, and a few rijstafel (rice table: small portions of several dishes for a table to share). Dining solo, a rijstafel was out of the question, but the ayam penggang seten caught my eye.I'm pretty sure the literal translation of the dish is "fried chicken in Satan sauce", which seemed apt: this was one of the most brutally spicy dishes I've ever eaten. Aside from the intense heat, the dish was actually very flavourful, with garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and other spices shining through. Every entree here comes with a number of small side dishes: white rice, pickled veggies, veggies in a coconut curry sauce, and fried tempeh. Everything was delicious, all the better when washed down with a glass of Bintang (an Indonesian beer).The staff was friendly, but harried.

Name: David N.
Review: With a significant Indonesian population in Amsterdam, we made it a point to partake while we were visiting. We tried making a reservation online for a Monday evening, but nothing was available, so we decided to chance it and walk-in anyway. We arrived to a busy, but not quite full, restaurant and were seated right away. Our first impressions were of awe and appreciation: the interior was slick yet classy, simple but tasteful. We were also delighted that most of the staff was lgbt =)We love spicy, so at the recommendation of our server, we ordered the Kuning Rice Table. Why not try a little of everything? The next hour was an explosion of flavor that would leave us reminiscing for days. From the shrimp soup appetizer to the amazing array of skewers to the spiced coconut to the classic rendang...everything was wonderfully seasoned, cooked, and presented. At about 30 euros/person, it wasn't a cheap meal, but it was definitely worth it as a delicious treat.We ended up cleaning our plates and left fully stuffed and satisfied. The entire waitstaff was friendly, helpful, and wore shining smiles. We definitely recommend this fantastic restaurant, and we look forward to returning in the near future!

Name: Amanda C.
Review: Came here with reservations. The entrance was confusing as there's not host to greet you there, but halfway through the front of the seatings, you'll then find the host. It felt weird to walk through people looking for the hostess. Upon arrival we let them know we had a reservation and they sat us a few minutes after. They're super busy here so catching their attention for water and drinks was a bit tough. We went with their set menu for two people versus picking our own dishes; which to me is super helpful! We had the Celebes Rijsttafel for 34.5€ each person. We ordered a lumpia and soup, but we both got soup :/ it was a good kick of spice but got too spicy for me to finish. This set came with:- steamed rice- fried rice: tasty and had crispy bits in it.- tender braised beef in spicy chili sauce: this had a small kick to it, but not unbearable. The beef was soft and flavorful.- grilled chicken in green pepper sauce: the green sauce was too spicy for me so i only ate a small bit of the chicken without the sauce. It wasn't enough for me to judge the dish, but the chicken wasn't dry.- skewer of lemongrass with minced fish- chicken skewer: tasty!- beef skewer: flavor was good.- cod fish: i liked this as it was crispy on the edges of the fish and soft inside. - beans with bamboo shoots: not usually a can of bamboo but i didn't taste it. The bits of tofu were also yummy:- fried soybean cake: these came out like chips but also very bland in flavor.- cucumber salad: i love pickled cucumbers so this dish was yummy and finished before the meal started.- mango salad: this was cooked with veggies that look like cole slaw, but i enjoyed picking out the bits of mango to eat.- spiced coconut: i loved putting these bits on top of my rice for every bite or even on top of any of the dishes. It adds yumminess to every bite.- nutcrackers: this was the sweet, crunchy dish that didn't go well with the meal because it was a sweeter dish than all savory dishes with it. Also felt like crispy nuts. Overall, busy spot right where the flower market is. Entrance could be better and more welcoming as well. It was around 84€ total for two people with 2 glasses of wine and a bottle of water. However, they asked for service so i felt obligated to tip and rounded it to 90€.

Name: Christine W.
Review: If you're a tourist in Amsterdam you might be thinking that you should try more typical Amsterdam foods BUT here's why you need to try out sampurna+++it's authentic - at least according to the bf who is from indonesia. We got the batara menu which like most of the other menus allowed a large variety of food sampling. If you aren't sure what to get, that's a greAt menu- faves were the chicken soup/fried dumplings/salad with light vinegrette +++the flavors were such an adventure- each dish was a delightful combo of a lot of tastes, spicy/fragrant/savory/even a hint of sweetness +++dessert was delicious - we got the es pisang goreng which is a fried plantain with delicious vanilla ice cream and whipped cream

Name: John M.
Review: "Rice Table" is a uniquely Indonesian meal I like to enjoy in Amsterdam.  This trip my hotel is by the Flower Market so when I looked for Indonesian, I was pleased to find a highly rated restaurant so close by. We arrived at 7:30pm on a Saturday without a reservation and were seated with the condition we would be done by 8:30.  After us, everyone without a reservation was turned away.Even though they needed to have us finished by 8:30 the service was prompt but not pushy.The rice was great, consisting of a bowl of safron rice along with about a dozen small bowls of assorted meats and vegetables.  The food varied from mild to moderatly spicy and was perfectly filling for two people.

Name: Mark K.
Review: First time eating Indonesian food and I was lucky enough to eat it in Amsterdam.  I would recommend this place because the folks are friendly and the food was really good.  I have to say that I didn't know what to make of it because the flavors were very unique to this Californian's taste buds.  The closest resemblance in my mind would be Thai food.  But they are not siblings in taste, but more like distant cousins.

Name: Eva K.
Review: When I think of Amsterdam, I think of all the Indonesian food I'm going to get there.Living in Copenhagen where there is none makes me craving for food from my homeland now and then, with the closest restaurant being in Hamburg, I was almost high (no pun intended) with excitement when I knew that we were going to Amsterdam for study trip held by the company.Sampurna is right by the flower market, it's fortunately within walking distance from our hotel in Spuistraat and it's open until very late and that's a win for us because we arrived at our hotel quite late and we could still score late dinner.Warning: Service is very slow, you need to be proactive to get the menu card and order because they're very understaffed, but apart from that - I have no complaints. Heck, I didn't even take one star off it because the food is simply amazing.If you're two people who share same interest with food, go for the rijstaffel. I know, I know - they might not seem to be the most authentic choice to make, but rijstaffel here is where you actually get to sample all the dishes in the menu. They come in mini-plates for two, so it's not something that they made up for the Dutch consumption. I chose the vegetarian rijstaffel that I shared with my friend. I am not vegetarian but I don't eat poultry and most of other rijstaffel has chicken on it, so vegetarian is fine by me and it turned out it was the best choice. I was overwhelmed with the amount of dishes keep coming to our table, tofu satay, orek tempe, sambal goreng telor, lodeh, gado gado... amazing. They tasted amazing as well. Only one thing negative is that the rice came in a very small bowl and I thought it was free to refill, but unfortunately you pay for the refill, small charge, but still - it would have been nice with free rice refill, you being in Indonesian restaurant and all, but don't let it discourage you. If you're in Amsterdam and you want to sample Indonesian food, this is the place to go!

Name: Emma W.
Review: Great food and amazing service.I'm not a good writer and don't know how to write hundreds of words in admiration of a place but I must say that it was better than expectations. I ordered a Tomato soup and Goat cheese croquettes for a warm starter and for the main course I had a steak. The quantity was good but I guess they can work a bit more on the quality of the ingredients. Also, the staff was very friendly and professional.

Name: Daniel K.
Review: Stoped in just to see if we could get a table, they were very accomidating and the wait was small.  The food was extreemly good the bitterballen was fantastic. As I am not from the area I wanted to try lots of different thing and the Combination plate was had a little of all of their main dishes, it is a must try.The service was awsome even though it was packed

Name: Robin M.
Review: The Pantry is a cozy place. Yes , it's small but they have a few tables outside as well.  You will need a reservation here !!! The service was quite friendly and the server patiently explained the different dishes. They offer a regular menu in many languages and four 3 course menus . We found ordering from them a good way to sample many things.  They offer a combination hutspot which puts the 3 different types of mashed potatoes on the same plate as the meatball or sausage so you can sample all 3. Our favorite was the mash with the sauerkraut !  We also had the fish which was fresh and simple. The 3 course menu includes a starter - the pea soup was outstanding - and dessert.  The stroopwafel with caramel ice cream was very very good ! Enough to share also. If you choose something with a different dessert , I'd pay extra to change it or order it a la carte. Ordering this way was cost effective and it was plenty of food.  The Pantry is a good choice when looking for authentic Dutch cuisine.

Name: Johanna S.
Review: It is not easy to find a traditional dutch food restaurant in the netherlands. But, i now found it. The restaurant prepares the food i ate while growing up. While surrounded by a kitsch amount of dutch painting and delft plue tile and dutch music on the radio, i enjoyed a steak.Hostsare friendly, and prices are ok. Definitely will take some visiting overseas friends here.

Name: Tamuna U.
Review: Small restaurant serving traditional Dutch food - get reservations to avoid waiting!!Got the following:Bitterballen: 4 stars, piping hot and full of flavor. Could make a meal out of these. Enjoyed the pairing with whole grain mustardOven bake with ground meat and cauliflower: 3 stars, tasty, but unremarkable. Needed salt. I stole some braised cabbage from my husband and that made it taste a lot betterBeef stew: 3 stars, came with mashed potatoes and braised cabbage. The cabbage was 5 stars. The rest again was tasty but unremarkable, and needed some punchThe dessert was the best: 5 stars. White chocolate mousse and chocolate ice cream, in addition to a little eggnog custard and fresh whipped cream. Delicious

Name: Jamie J.
Review: When people ask me where I went on my European vacation, I say London, Amsterdam, Germany, and Switzerland!  It reality, it was only London for 3 days and Amsterdam for 1.  Since we didn't have a lot of time in Amsterdam, we really needed to make our meals count.  We decided on The Pantry for our dinner.Our last stop was at the Royal Palace, so we had some walking to do from there.  It's not far, but it is a little bit of a walk.  However, Amsterdam is so beautiful, I didn't mind the scenery while walking.  The restaurant is located in an alley, so it's not really off a street with cars.  Even at 5:30pm, the restaurant had about an hour wait.  Apparently, a waiting list is not something they do at many restaurants we visited in Amsterdam (we tried going to 3 different places for lunch and all of them didn't have one).  Instead, you just wait outside.  This day, we got lucky because someone cancelled their reservation.  Instead of 45 minutes, it ended up being 15.  Yes!!!The place is small, so it is a little cramped.  Was it uncomfortable?  Not at all.  However, you are really close to the next table.  Before I get to the food, let's talk a little bit about the service.  It is awesome!  Don't let anybody tell you Dutch people don't have good customer service.  I saw a video on Youtube, before coming to Amsterdam, that says the service here is not the same as in America.  Probably not.  It may not be a good barometer of all restaurants in Amsterdam, but The Pantry definitely has great customer service.  Now for the food.  I saved the food review for last, because it would take me 4 hours to write this part.  I can't even come close to saying these items, let alone spelling them.  Anyway, we started with Bitterballen, which is like a fried meatball stuffed with gravy.  Freakin' brilliant!  Seriously, what's not to like?  For our entrées, we had Boerenkoolstamppot (smoked sausage with mashed potatoes mixed with Kale), combination of the Boerenkoolstamppot, along with Hutspot (mashed potatoes mixed with stewed beef, carrots and onions), and Zuurkoolstamppot (mashed potatoes mixed with sauerkraut), and the Savory Beef and Onion Stew, which is served with red cabbage and regular mashed potatoes.  My daughters got the Boerenkoolstamppot, which they both loved.  However, they took my regular mashed potatoes and I took the kale ones.  My wife got the combo and she liked that one, but liked my Beef Stew better.  While we all switched and tried everyone else's food, everybody loved the entire meal.

Name: Mimi S.
Review: Forgot where I found out about The Pantry, probably on TripAdvisor. Great spot to grab traditional Dutch food. The Pantry is a small, cozy place with amazing ambience and service.We came in for an early dinner after a long day of walking around. This was one of our favorite spots in Amsterdam! Great selection of dishes and drinks. First time trying bitterballen and it was great. SO got the combination hutspot and I got the oven dish (cauliflower, beef, cheese, mashed potatoes). We loved our experience here!Would also recommend the Apple Bandit cider which was quite refreshing and not too sweet; it was better than expected.

Name: Andy N.
Review: A visit to The Pantry was a must for us on our first day back in Amsterdam. With an impressively no-frills name and a quaint environment, we were happy to see it serve some delicious Dutch food while having all-around great service.We came in a little after they had just opened up for the day and an array of lunch specials were presented to us. While our main objective coming here was to try their Hutspot, we decided their €21 set which included pea-soup and a custard dessert would be more appropriate. Thank goodness too because everything was tasty and splendid.The pea-soup with rye bread and smoked ham was one of the best I had tasted in a lifetime. It was thick and not overly salty when it comes to pea soup, and their homemade rye was a great accompaniment.The main dish came with their signature hutspot along with two other mashes accompanying either a smoked sausage or meatball. Since there were two of us, we each got a separate meat so we were able to try both. Personally, the meatball was my winner, which is funny because we both enjoyed each other's meats better (lol). All in all, it was fantastic to taste the different mashed potato concoctions on the side- my favorite being the one mixed in with kale.Our vanilla yoghurt with custard was simply divine and a great way to end our meal. Dare I say it- I liked this portion the best out of everything we tried during our lunch set!I was very impressed with the service and food quality here at The Pantry and would absolutely recommend it for everyone to try visiting Amsterdam.

Name: Tibs C.
Review: Good service, ambiance, food presentation. I think it's a solid place to try traditional Dutch food, just my taste buds aren't impressed by most European fare.They have preset menu choices which is nice. From menu 1, my favorite was the pea soup with sausage. The stamppot (sausage over different mashed potatoes) was just ok to me, several reviews laud the sauerkraut mash, and if you love sauerkraut you'll probably quite like it (alas, not a fan here). Dessert was a light yogurt/custard. One of my friends tried menu 2 which featured croquettes, something resembling shepherd's pie, and poffertjes (mini pancakes). All decent, and very good portion sizes (none of us were able to finish everything), and I'd say definitely worth a visit if you're on vacation and want to sample Dutch food.

Name: Alyssa W.
Review: The Pantry is a great traditional little Dutch restaurant. My boyfriend and I walked in around 7PM and were seated quickly (if you have a party bigger than two, you should probably make a reservation). The place is dimly lit, small, but very cozy and bustling. I got a hutspot dish which is mashed potatoes mixed with stewed beef, carrots and onions and served with a smoked sausage. My boyfriend ordered "Menu 1" which is a full course meal: appetizer - pea soup with rye bread and smoked bacon, entree - a combination of hutspot, zuurkoolstamppot (mash potatoes with sauerkraut),  boerenkoolstamppot (mashed potatoes with kale) served with a smoked sausage or a meatball, and dessert - vanilla custard with yogurt and syrup. I'm not a fan of heavy food, but I really enjoyed the hutspot and the boerenkoolstamppot, but not so much the sauerkraut one. I also am generally indifferent about sausage and would not care for a large sausage as I had here. It was so good - the smokiness really made it great and tastes nothing like the hot dog flavor that I was scared to get. We also ordered the apple pie because hey, Dutch dessert! It was a really interesting texture, crunchy on the top, unlike the famous apple pie from Winkel 43, but nonetheless delicious and I enjoyed it much more than any apple pie that I have had in the States! The vanilla custard with yogurt dessert was rather disappointing though because it literally tasted like... cup yogurt from the supermarket and the syrup was really fake tasting. Overall a satisfying experience with attentive service.

Name: Earl H.
Review: Amsterdam isn't exactly a culinary wonderland but it has some local flavors you shouldn't miss. The Pantry serves up typical Dutch cuisine with some of the friendliest service you'll find in Amsterdam.   I went for the zuurkoolstamppot which is Sauerkraut mixed into mashed potatoes with a sausage. Nothing exciting to look at but it was actually pretty delicious. If you're in Amsterdam I'd highly recommend making reservations and give the pantry a shot.

Name: Lindsay S.
Review: Food was delicious, service was great, prices were standard!We thoroughly enjoyed our dinner here and will be back next time we visit Amsterdam. We made reservations the night before and glad we did because there was a small wait. We were lucky to get a nice outdoor table. Wine and beers were brought in a timely manner to our table after ordering. The bitterballen appetizer was fantastic. We scarfed it down in seconds it seemed. We contemplated ordering more. Hah. For our dinners we ordered the hutspot (which was to die for) and the sea bass. I wish we had just ordered the hutspot for both entrees. The fish seemed a little overpriced for the quality but it was good still. After dinner we ordered the apple pie and cinnamon ice cream. Both were great! We will definitely be back for more. Only con for me was wait time but it's worth the wait!

Name: Bryan W.
Review: Forgot where I found out about The Pantry, probably on TripAdvisor. Great spot to grab traditional Dutch food. The Pantry is a small, cozy place with amazing ambience and service.We came in for an early dinner after a long day of walking around. This was one of our favorite spots in Amsterdam! Great selection of dishes and drinks. First time trying bitterballen and it was great. SO got the combination hutspot and I got the oven dish (cauliflower, beef, cheese, mashed potatoes). We loved our experience here!Would also recommend the Apple Bandit cider which was quite refreshing and not too sweet; it was better than expected.

Name: Amber H.
Review: Got extremely lucky when coming here last night. Couldn't call for a reservation as we didn't have a local number and our receptionist wouldn't help us out we decided to walk over.There was a table of 6 leaving and the place was full. We got seated and was served right away. I got the french onion soup, amazing ! It was perfect the onions and the cheese well done. The steak was good but the few veggies that came with it weren't fully cooked. The lamb was juicy and the veggies were packed with garlic and spices. What a treat this place is. We also got the beef carpaccio it was made well and flavourful.We kept seeing other dishes people were ordering in the restaurant and we all wanted to try the duck or the escargots they were huge !  If you do go here know that they have their own aquarium downstairs with oysters and lobsters right beside the kitchen and the bathrooms, but do be careful those stairs are serious business extremely steep.

Name: David H.
Review: I was seated at the bar for dinner and immediately I knew I was going to have a great experience when I overheard the owner/manager say to a waiter, "You see, the two guys at your table that shared a meal and great conversation, and time together--that is why we do what we do. " And the meal was in par with that care and hospitality.

Name: JR R.
Review: I visited the restaurant on Mid September 2018 at night with a group of 6. It was my first night in town and read online that it served local dishes, had good reviews and was close to our Hotel, so I decided to give it a try. My plate choice was the Classic Beef Stew which was really good. The other guests were satisfied as well with their orders, who had Dutch traditional and non-traditional dishes. The restaurant had Jopen IPA on draft and a couple other Dutch beers, which were served at the right temperature.The waiter was friendly and provided good service. The prices were fair, particularly considering the location and ambience, which can be described as darkish, and cozy yet spacious. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, but I found the indoors more appealing. If you wanna try Dutch food and are close by, I certainly recommend you considering visiting it.

Name: Hsiao-Ting C.
Review: 4.5 stars We were looking for a place to eat and went to three places before we found one that had seatings with no wait. I didn't have much expectation on the food since there was no wait. Who would have known the food was actually pretty good! My husband have been trying beef stew on this trip and thought this one made it the best. My lamb chops were cooked perfectly. It's a pretty big space but we had to fold up our stroller and hold our baby during the meal but the staff were really nice. You should come here if you want a taste of Dutch food!

Name: Anco M.
Review: We went with 30 for a work related dinner to Van Speyk. A casual place where we were offered a three course menu with a choice for starter and mains. The food was excellent excellent, the service friendly, though, with such a big group, not very quick. Well worth coming back to.

Name: Quinn V.
Review: Great friendly service. We got the scallops and the soup to start. They were good. We got the duck confit which was crispy outside but very dry inside. We ordered the steak medium rare. Could have been better seasoned. Creme brûlée was fine. For €€€ I would expect a bit more on the entrées

Name: Scott G.
Review: Had an awesome meal. Sanne took great care of us. She was very patient and helpful. One member of our party has an emotional allergy to mayonaise and Sanne made sure he did not get in trouble.  Adam and Wayne had a gr8 view for the entire evening and were nothing but smiles.Adam and Wayne had the escargot por duo.  I had the Dutch oysters which were awesome.For dinner we had Adam (lobster which the chef deshelled for adam), WAYNE(Entrecote with champignon sauce), Scott was blown away by the sudderlapjes(Dutch stew).  We finished up with some Irish coffee and a nice apple desert.  Looking forward to a return if ever in Amsterdam again.  To quote the great Rick flair.... Wooooooo!

Name: Rob B.
Review: Beautiful little place located close to Crown Plaza and the Renaissance hotel. A reservation is a must. Typical Dutch style service. We loved the scallops and the steak. While the pork chops was nicely seasoned it was so over cooked that it was difficult to cut and more so to eat. To be fair, they said it would be fully done and that was an understatement. Warning, the stairs to the restrooms are only for agile rock climbers.

Name: Andrea T.
Review: The first night we arrived at the Crowne Plaza, we asked the concierge for a dinner suggestion.  He said Van Speyk.  However, we wanted to walk some of the city so we decided to venture away from this area.  We came back the next night (a Friday).  The decor of this restaurant is very nice.  Beautiful chandeliers hang from the ceiling.We had a group of 3 and were promptly seated.  I do not think this is normal as the night prior, the place was full when we walked past.  I think it would be best to make a reservation.We had a huge lunch so I wanted something a bit lighter for dinner.  I opted for the sea bass dish.  My colleagues had the venison and duck.  The food came out rather quickly which was nice.  My sea bass was delicious!  Everything on the plate was great!  My colleagues also said their dishes were great!We ordered dessert.  I had the White Chocolate Cheesecake which was light and fluffy with delicious berries on the top.We thoroughly enjoyed this dining experience.

Name: Jaswinder K.
Review: Waking in the ambience was perfect for my husbands pre birthday dinner. This place does reservations so you might not get lucky on a Saturday evening. Fortunately there was a table for 2 opened and were seated immediately. The service was impeccable; we were first seated with some lover butter and bread. The waiter came over and offered for us to taste the wine. So I ordered the beef stew and truffle fries. My husband ordered the duck with spinach. The food was delicious if you want to have a nice fancy dinner out with your date I would take them here !!

Name: Mister B.
Review: Good location near the Amsterdam Central train station.  We had a great Van Speyk salad and a rack of lamb and a Dutch stew.  We were happy with each.Good English speaking service and menu.  Go to their website to make a reservation.  Tables filled up quickly after 7 pm.

Name: MrnMrs G.
Review: We ate here TWICE and once at their other location... does that tell you something? DELISH!Although seating was cramped, the meal was amazingly good (veggie breakfast and espresso drinks especially) - and guess what, you'll eventually get used to those strangers being THAT close to you while you enjoy your meal... maybe. This place is always busy so either get here for breakfast right when they open or test your luck! Haha!

Name: Ruth F.
Review: I think this place is a little over priced and just OK. They don't take reservations and the wait was around 40 minutes both times we stopped by (on weekdays).Staff was friendly and food was OK, nothing spectacular.

Name: Michael D.
Review: It looked nicer than it tasted. The food was bland. The coffee was very good. The place itself and staff were nice._____

Name: Kevin C.
Review: My son was hungry was we needed a quick place where we can grab him some to go.  Reviews on yelp for this place was glowing.  When we got there, we had a positive vibe and understood how many people would love this place.  It was quite busy but the staffs were nice.  I ordered a short stack (3) pancakes which had raspberry along with blueberry and bananas topping.  It came with two maple syrups.  While the presentation was there, my son and I felt the pancakes themselves were quite heavy.  I would've expected them to be more fluffier.  But that was really the only con.  I am sure if we ordered and dined in and tried other dishes, I would enjoy their food.  But for today, my review is solely based on those pancakes.  To their credit, we did hear from other tourists we met on an excursion that they loved the place.  :)

Name: Dayna S.
Review: We were refused service and made fun of because we were Americans. We wanted a drink and everyone at the bar was drinking (it was 10pm) and they repeated over and over that the kitchen was "closed" even though everyone at the bar was drinking. It was clear that they only wanted Dutch people in their bar. I had to assist my friend in the bathroom and they commented that if two people were in the restroom they would "see it on the cameras." I felt offended and upset after leaving this bar. They could have handled the situation with more respect. Would NOT recommend to tourists.

Name: Kristian A.
Review: The food tasted great and was very filling. They brought out bread also which I used for those dipping sauces. It came with a small salad which was alright nothing special. The ribs tasted amazing. Preferred the regular over the smoked but still great. The only real negative is it is extremely expensive. Came to about 40 euros a person and that's a mixed rib meal and a beer. And then if you use credit card they charge an extra 5% FYI. Was told it's usually a long wait here and they send you across the street to drink until something opens up. But we got there early around 4pm and sat outside. Around 530pm when we left there was a wait. Seating outside you may be sitting back to back with another table so if your shy try to sit inside.

Name: Leo M.
Review: Racist... I'm Asian... Walked in there asking how long the wait is.. there's about 3-4 groups waiting outside. A man with a "menu" on his shirt with glasses in the late 40s looked and yelled to my face that "For you, 3 hours". "I'm sorry?" "Yea, 3 hours for you."I heard of this place from multiple Vloggers... I'm no longer interested after that conversation..

Name: Edward W.
Review: Walked in around 6pm and luckily managed to snag 2 spots at the bar right away. Our hostel host suggested the ribs here, so we went with the mixed ribs. The beef ribs were fantastic and tasted especially good with the tomato mayo. I thought the pork ribs were okay and could have done without. Plenty of meat on the pork ribs and meat wasn't too tough, but I just thought the smoked and charred beef tasted much better. Also ordered an Amstel beer to quench my thirst and it went very well with the ribs. Light beer that didn't mask the taste of the meat and actually complimented it well. Overall very enjoyable experience although our server was a little rude when taking our order. Also smaller groups tend to get seated much faster. We were seated right next to the entrance and heard lots of 4+ groups get told the wait would be 1 hour+, but individuals or groups of 2 were almost seated immediately.

Name: Kelvin C.
Review: I think I came in here expecting something else, which was good ole fashioned-smoked american ribs slathered in tangy BBQ sauce.  Well, this wasn't it.  It's actually everything I stated above sans the BBQ sauce.  Instead they serve it with Hollandaise sauce as well as a side of Hollandaise "bbq" sauce...which is basically Hollandiase with a little bit of ketchup (I think).  The ribs were definitely smoked well and the meat was a bit leaner than what I'm used to so they don't fall of the bone.  Also, they provide you a MASSIVE amount of food for the price so if you order the mixed ribs plate, it is more than enough for two.  We also tried the french onion soup, which turned out to be better than what we had in france, and the tomato bisque soup, which was decent.  TIP: For a party of 2, don't be put off if the host tells you there is a two hour wait.  He's completely overestimating in order to weed out the curious people walking in that don't want to commit.  Simply head over to their bar right across the street and he'll come grab you in 45 minutes tops.4 stars.

Name: Sofia D.
Review: This place was so busy I didn't think I would get in but to my luck again, there was one empty table all the way in the back at around 9pm. In Amsterdam you literally have to make a reservation at most restaurants because you will not get into anything good until past 9-10. Take note of that. There's only a few tables here and the rest is just a wrap around bar top where everyone gathers. Service was good. I seen a lot of complaints in the other reviews about the servers . Yeah, some people could get offended at some of the things they say but I found it quite amusing. I'm a bit of a smart ass myself so it wasn't anything I couldn't handle. There was a comment made, I threw one back, we all laughed and it was all happy days from there. Do yourself a favor and just get the regular ribs, not smoked. I got the mixed platter and while both of the ribs were tasty, the smoked were a bit tough and had way less meat. Regular ribs all the way. Way more meat and fall right off the bone. They were awesome.It comes with coleslaw and bread and I also ordered a baked potato on the side. It came with garlic butter inside that was absolutely delicious. A Dutch beer to wash it all down with and I was good to go. It's a lot of food. I had someone to share it with. There's no way I could have eaten it all by myself. I wish I could have came again and tried the lamb shoulder. Next time I'm in Amsterdam.

Name: Joyce S.
Review: This place is always busy but it may not seem like it because they send everyone across the street to have a drink while they put you on the wait list. (Honestly, I think they do that so you can bring your money to their other spot for some drinks.) However, I opted to not do that and just decided to wait outside. And yup, me and my boyfriend were the only ones that didn't feel obligated to go to their  cafe/bar for drinks. I didn't care cause I just wanted to eat their ribs!! I guess the host felt weird that we just stood outside so our 40 minute wait turned into 10 minute wait LOL. Lucky us! Inside is kind of dark and pub like. But it smelled good inside since they had an open kitchen where they grilled their ribs! We sat at the bar and we could see where they grilled the ribs. It looked amazing! We got the mixed rib for two people and we were stuffed! I don't know how people can eat a whole thing themselves. The both ribs were good and tender. The salad was nice for a fresh crunch. The baked potato was a nice side when you need a break from the meat. Overall, this is a good place if you want some good ribs! Service was only so-so. Sitting at the bar allowed me to see who got better treatment. But again, I just came for their food :).

Name: Andrew G.
Review: After reading all the reviews we thought we should try it.  Upon arrival we waited around 10min before seated,  it wasn't particularly busy but would have been nice to be acknowledged at some point.  The smoked ribs were very salty,  the cole slaw was great,  overall a mediocre at best experience.  The steak was also average, and the baked potato was good. I would not eat here again,  cost of the meal was quite high.

Name: Bobby S.
Review: Food was good and would definitely recommend it. We were disappointed with the service. Long wait times and at the end, the server forced us to tip. I did bring to notice the average service and he came up with some excuse to justify it.

Name: Adri P.
Review: My. God. The ribs fall off the bone!!! And you're given plenty. The mac n cheese in the cheesiest and creamiest ever (hello Dutch cheese), and the garlic broccoli is amazing and so fresh. Staff was super friendly and welcoming. There was a bit of a wait, but no more than 10 minutes and well worth it. Food came quickly once seated. And it was nice and hot!Typing this as I try to recover. Can't breathe. Unbuttoning pants... hoping to digest for round 2.

Name: Ivy C.
Review: 3.5 in actuality. It honestly isn't bad. We came here from a referral. The wait was about 45 minutes, not bad we went next door to the Coffeeshop and chilled there till it was time for our table. We got seated outside in a really tiny shared table. It was fine. We ordered ribs, a steak and a beef tartar. The beef tartar was decent, nothing amazing as far as beef tartars go. We asked for the steak to be medium rare but I'm positive it was rare, but still pretty good and flavorful. The ribs was the one thing I was looking forward to the most!! It looked super appetizing. But when u cut into it, it's pretty dry despite how beautifully it falls off the bone. Pretty disappointed in that. The red wine is disgusting don't get that.

Name: Stefanie B.
Review: This review is for the guy working the front the evening of 4/24/19 around 11:30pm, who should not be working in customer service.We walked in, said we were a party of 3 people, his response... "Full". "Ok, soo how long is the wait?" "Full." "All night?"He rolls his eyes, shrugs and says, "like an hour."Ok... so we turn around because his attitude was nauseating and he goes, "k BYE."Did you want us to gravel at your feet podium man?We travel from Los Angeles twice a year, entertaining artists and agents; always take them here but we won't if you are going to have the customer service skills of a barn animal. Also the quality has declined since we started coming here several years ago. Beef tartare is good but the burgers were too undercooked last time (it was just too much raw meat going on) and the ribs were dried out and took forever because they accidentally dropped them... and then brought another table their order which included ribs. So by the time I got my burger it was cold.

Name: Michael J.
Review: Food was alright. They were out of the item that I really wanted so I got the burger with pulled pork on it. Beer was so so. Service wasn't great but I'd go back. I'd give a 3.5 star if I could.

Name: Maria F.
Review: They certainly don't skimp on the meals; I couldn't finish the massive burger I was served. Food was really good. The place was crowded, but we lucked out on our timing: we didn't have a reservation but there was one free table. Would come back again. I wouldn't call this a "family friendly" place: it was mostly a younger, singles crowd, dark interior, louder background music. But older kids (10 and up) would be fine.

Name: Suzanne J.
Review: The decor was kinda cool and morbid. But the service was quite slow. Our server must have realised he'd left us for ages, because he did apologise. At least we had our drinks to sup whilst he was away. We looked on at other tables eating with a bit of longing. We decided to go for the Ribs since they were so highly rated on Yelp. We could see that this was the dish of choice for most in the restaurant. It was a massive board full of ribs that also came with a pot of mayo and a pot of BBQ. The meat was tender and tasty. I wouldn't say it's the best I've ever had. Or anywhere near that. But they were good. If they could have fell away at the bone a bit more, I would have loved them more.We ordered some fries to share. Sadly they were like crisps. Maybe that's how the Dutch eat chips? I couldn't eat it anyway and left them.It was quite expensive for what it is. I wouldn't go back.

Name: Todd F.
Review: The hamburgers in this place were beyond amazing. The hamburger special was a combination of ingredients you'd have to be mad to try, but somehow it unified into a coherent whole that was delicious. Macaroni and cheese was good, fries were good. If you can eat here, consider yourself lucky.

Name: Penny L.
Review: Having visited a similar concept in Lisbon I was really excited to check this place out.Walking through a shopping arcade we approached the food court  where we used the hand sanitizer provided and checked in online for covid purposes. The way it works..wonder round the one way system (not everyone adhered to this) check out the stalls, sit your arse back down and bring up a menu by scanning a QR code. Once you tap your selection and paid online  the food will be then delivered to your table. The stalls offered the following,  pizza,  meatballs,  smoothies,  tarts,  Mexican food, American wings, fish, greek and tapas. The prices extinguished the street food vibes but saying that Amsterdam is expensive. I chose the meatballs and a lemon tart. Himself chose the beef rolls in gelatinous rice and the pecan tart.  With a drink each this came to like €40.The food was delivered promptly,  the meatballs were forgettable and the tart miniscule.  The rolls were the best value although they contained lots of fresh mint which my partner hates haha Overall I would skip this place if I were you and treat yourself to a proper sit down meal

Name: Louisa M.
Review: Food Halls are a major draw for me no matter where in the world I travel, so I found De Foodhallen on Yelp and set out on foot to check it out. That was strike one for me. This place is far on the outskirts of town, it took me almost an hour of walking in crummy weather to finally reach it and when I did, it was not a fun experience. This is a very locals type place. I wouldn't go so far as to say it's unfriendly to tourists, but we weren't exactly welcomed. The Food Hall was an absolute madhouse, totally packed with people. I couldn't walk without bumping into somebody, and then I'd get an annoyed look and a sneer if I said "excuse me." It was so unpleasant. We were starving and ended up at the one booth that didn't have a massive line -- one with gourmet hot dogs. We ordered the most interesting sounding one on the menu: a spicy sausage topped with bacon and fried potatoes in a pretzel style bun.Once our food was ready, it was time to jockey for a seat. We couldn't find one anywhere. Most of the tables didn't have chairs, they were just high top "shelves" where you stand and eat. Nope, nobody would make enough space for us to squeeze in. So we had to go outside and stand and eat in the rain. There was no other option, and it made an unpleasant experience boil right over the edge. The food we had was good but very expensive, and I felt like an outsider in this part of the city. Normally I don't get those unwelcome vibes, but I did here. I'll probably go back and check this place out next time I'm in Amsterdam, though, but only very early on a sunny weekday, not a crowded weekend.

Name: Matthew L.
Review: Having visited a similar concept in Lisbon I was really excited to check this place out.Walking through a shopping arcade we approached the food court  where we used the hand sanitizer provided and checked in online for covid purposes. The way it works..wonder round the one way system (not everyone adhered to this) check out the stalls, sit your arse back down and bring up a menu by scanning a QR code. Once you tap your selection and paid online  the food will be then delivered to your table. The stalls offered the following,  pizza,  meatballs,  smoothies,  tarts,  Mexican food, American wings, fish, greek and tapas. The prices extinguished the street food vibes but saying that Amsterdam is expensive. I chose the meatballs and a lemon tart. Himself chose the beef rolls in gelatinous rice and the pecan tart.  With a drink each this came to like €40.The food was delivered promptly,  the meatballs were forgettable and the tart miniscule.  The rolls were the best value although they contained lots of fresh mint which my partner hates haha Overall I would skip this place if I were you and treat yourself to a proper sit down meal

Name: Phil N.
Review: I've never been super impressed by food markets and de Foodhallen didn't impress me either. It is very nicely decorated and worth going just to walk around. There are other halls in the same building too.We went at night and it was pretty crowded. It was difficult to find a table so if you're going with friends, one person should claim an open table while the others get the food.We got the Dutch Meatballs and the beef balls from de BallenBar. The meatballs had good flavor but were pretty salty. It was hard to eat more than two of these. The beef balls didn't taste like beef at all. I did like the texture of the well-fried exterior and the smooth interior. It was pretty bland so I was glad we got the truffle sauce. That really saved the balls and made it taste pretty good.

Name: Samantha L.
Review: While I love the food hall concept itself, the food stands were extremely disappointing.I strolled through the entire hall before picking a few to dine from. I had a nice margherita pizza and took interest in a patisserie stand. The rest weren't worth the money or the calories. Skip the Spanish tapas. The ramen was the worst! It was essentially soy sauce and water, there was no real developed flavor.Better for drinks and hanging out.

Name: Lydia A.
Review: I walked a million miles to get here bc it cameUp as a go to food market. I finally found it (tucked away in an alley). Honestly there wasn't anything special. There are various vendors (Thai, Indian, froyo, tacos, dim sum, sushi, beer, hotdogs, burgers, etc.) but it reminded me of all things I could get in the US. I got these bitterball fried balls which were actually pretty good but pricey at 7 dollars for 5. I decided not to get anything else bc I felt like it was all pretty basic. The only place that sold water was the bar which was 3 Euros! Madness. Would've been nice if they sold more European style food or some sort of Dutch food

Name: Cynthia B.
Review: This place says it opens at 11 on Sundays. But if you come don't plan on eating- no one will actually take your order until 12.

Name: Debby N.
Review: Didn't live up to the hype. I was really excited to go here after seeing it mentioned by quite a few travel bloggers. It was alright. It's basically like a food court you'd find at a mall. There is a variety of food but in my opinion the food tasted average and some of the staff are kinda rude. I do think the bitterballen I got was pretty good, my boyfriend enjoyed his burger but my calamari was mediocre.

Name: Andrea W.
Review: Cool space, but it gets crowded with so many people. There was also a live band which made it difficult to chat. There are many choices of different international cuisines, but food is really pricey for small portions. I tried Viet View's spring rolls, Txosta's pintxos, and Lima's tacos, which were all just average. It's a good place to walk around to take a look, but I would recommend eating elsewhere.

Name: Dina M.
Review: I never knew Dutch food was so good! It's hardy but that's what you'd expect from your grandmothers cooking, as their name suggests and celebrates, Grandmothers. I was lucky to snag a table at opening without a reservation. Only in AMS for 30 hours my goal was to get a good idea of the food culture. Going by their recommendation I chose:Green Pea Soup with Bacon & sausage. This was soooo good! But the bread and garlic butter combo was so incredible I had to have it removed from my table to prevent me from eating it all, then asking for more. I craved this the next morning and almost went back! Stamppot/Hotchpatch Meatball, Sausage, Bacon on mash of Sauerkraut & Potato. Super hearty, too much for me to finish, but I'm okay with that. The meatball was my favorite, great flavor.  Suddervless Stewed Beef, served with Boiled Potatoes, & Red Cabbage. A savory dish that you spoon over the red cabbage and boiled potatoes to balance the flavor. Apple Pie oh my!  This was so good, and I can't say I'm even a fan of pies. The crust wasn't your average, it took me a minute to identify what it reminded me of, cobbler!  That's it, it reminded me of cobblers my great grandmother made. When in Amsterdam, Moeders is a must.

Name: Patrick L.
Review: Moeders is a fantastic restaurant in Amsterdam, but I'm giving it 3 stars because of the service. My friend and I came in one snowy night hoping to be seated. We didn't have a reservation but wouldn't have minded waiting a little bit. We came in at around 7, but the staff turned us away saying there was no seats available. The next day, my friend and I decided that it was still worth it to give it a shot and come here to eat, so we came early to ensure we'd get a seat, and we did. We were ready to order within 5 minutes, but we had to wait around 10 minutes before a waitress came to take our order. People who were seated after us had already ordered and they still did not come to us for a while.  We both ordered the stamppot (or hotchpotch). I got the vegetarian one and my friend got the original one. Read below for review on the food. After we were done eating, we wanted to leave to go explore other parts of Amsterdam, but we were stuck there. The waitresses did not come to us and we kept trying to stop them so we could pay. While that may seem rude of us, we sat there for at least 10 minutes before doing so. Paying was a breeze and we left shortly after. As for the food, both of us really enjoyed it. I thought that there could have been a little more stuff in it as towards the end, all I was eating were potatoes, but it still had good flavor and good portions. Overall 3 stars for service, 4 for food

Name: Mary-Jane A.
Review: Our first night in Amsterdam and this restaurant was recommended by the hotel we were staying at. Was not disappointed!  On the door it had a note saying that they were fully booked but to come in to see if they had any tables. Luckily they did and we ate outside as it was a very warm and sunny day. Once we ordered the food came up quite quickly. We ordered the hotch potch with spinach, the beef and onion stew and veg curry. They were all very tasty and quite filling. I found that there was a little too liberal sprinkling of salt, but I generally don't add that much in my meals. Otherwise so tasty!  Definitely do go for some good authentic Dutch food, it's worth a visit.

Name: Sheila G.
Review: It doesn't take a non-Dutch-speaking genius to figure out the meaning of Moeders.  All you have to do is walk inside:  instead of wallpaper, there are what must be a thousand framed pictures of -- mothers!  In this cozy, tea room-like ambiance, the rule of the day is Dutch home-style cooking, and it was very good.We ordered a carafe of wine, then tried to decipher the menu.  It wasn't a language problem, but one of perplexity.  Despite the crowded room, our server was unflappable and patient as she explained the setup.  We had a choice of three different fixed-price dinners, but there were also à la carte choices.  So after we ordered a carafe of wine, we settled on one full meat hotchpotch dinner, one à la carte vegetarian platter, and a Dutch pea soup, all to share.For the meat dinner we chose spinach as the vegetable, which seemed to be combined with mashed potatoes.  This was surrounded by a meatball, sausage, and bacon.  We were able to substitute an additional meatball for the sausage.  The vegetarian plate also had potatoes and cheese, with a delicious croquette instead of meat.The Dutch pea soup was a thick puree enhanced with diced sausage, very tasty, and served in an enameled covered crock.The one dessert that came with the full dinner was more than enough for two - a plate with two small cups of pudding/mousse, plus a center scoop of ice cream.A filling and satisfying meal in a lovely atmosphere, with excellent service, made this a memorable experience.

Name: Mike H.
Review: The food was just okay. Besides the spareribs (the only dish we liked), the other dishes were disappointing. The spinach mash potato in our hutspot was really dry to the point that I could hardly eat it without pouring and mixing with all of the gravy. The meat that came with it was definitely over salted. The Moeder's veggie tasted like Thai curry with a strong flavor from lemongrass. Even for rustic dining, food overall tasted one dimensional and lacked refinement. We also did not expect the place to be completely filled with tourists and seating arrangements to be so cramped that you constantly have move over for other guests to get by. It's not hard to tell that its popularity has overgrown its dining capacity over the years. Having said that, I wouldn't recommend going out of the way just to come here.

Name: Livia C.
Review: Visited Moeders based on online reviews and suggestions. Unfortunately our order was forgotten about, until many other tables seated after us had received mains and desserts, a waitress realised we were without food and then our meal was promptly served after that.. I ordered the traditional hotchpotch/stamppot in which the server asked if I wanted sauerkraut or spinach; I said sauerkraut but I'm not entirely sure where the sauerkraut came into play? The meatball and sausage were averagely cooked and unfortunately I didn't eat the bacon slice as I didn't trust the appearance. Very busy atmosphere, lines of people walking in, but I believe it is based on previous suggestions and many people would try once and not return. Overall I'd suggest you try once, but not return.

Name: Peter H.
Review: The Food? Let's just say during my 3 day stay in Amsterdam I returned 4 times... each day I got something different but for my first day I got their medley for two that brought an assortment of different meets and potatoes and stews (just to get a taste of what the Netherlands had to offer)... each day I ended my meals with they're apple pie... I know you may think you've had a better desert... but this Apple pie is like no other... I got there at 5pm when they opened and by the time I was finished with my meal the pie was fresh out of the oven... it was so good I returned 2 hrs later for another slice  I have NOTHING negative to say about this place except I wish they opened sooner so I could enjoy them for lunch as well . This right here is a hidden GEM in Amsterdam. I'm talking about   G E N U I N E   Dutch food from across the Netherlands in one, "made with love by moeder" location right on the canal... inside they have charming staff and pictures of hundreds (maybe even thousands) of pictures of all the mothers that have eaten at this restaurant. (If you come with your mum, take a picture of her and submit it to them- they will gladly add her beautiful profile to the wall of fame)

Name: Calvin Y.
Review: Perhaps my expectations were elevated because I love comfort food or perhaps it was my excitement for traditional dutch cuisine.  Waitstaff were friendly enough.  We had a reservation and got there earlier than expected, but they were nice enough to seat us half an hour before our reservation.  The reservation was nice as this place filled up fast.  The atmosphere was kitschy home decor and I loved watching the dumbwaiter bring food up.    Moeders was adequate for a check list item as a tourist, but I was not amazed given the price point for mashed potatoes, beef stew, and pickled red cabbage.

Name: M Y.
Review: Stopped by late in the evening. We were able to easily get a table for two. The interior is cozy and inviting. We ordered a few dishes including Mamma's happas, the Fisher's wife salad, and the pea soup. They were all delicious. I also really like the dishes they served the food in. Overall we had a great dining experience here. I'd definitely recommend having a meal at Moeders.

Name: Vicki L.
Review: Terrible terrible terrible customer service. Unless you want to be aggressively yelled at by a waitress here, don't bother coming.We came here as a walk in for dinner and this brusque waitress says "BOOKING NO BOOKING?" quickly. I couldn't hear her asked for a party of 2. She repeats again "BOOKING NO BOOKING!" And I said no booking and she said GO OUTSIDE. So I confusedly walk outside and don't see a designated area for waiting and blindly stand where I see some other girls standing who said they were also confused and waiting.Angry waitress lady comes back out and yells some vague words again and points. Everybody is super confused and doesn't know what's going on. She then comes back out and tries to take down names of people who are waiting... completely skipping the order of who showed up (she let some other get on the list ahead of me even though I was there first) and then started yelling at a group of 5 Chinese women saying she didn't have a table for 5. At this point I just decide to leave and go somewhere else because I'm not going to eat dinner in an environment that is so hostile regardless of how good the food might be. I'm not going to subject myself to that while eating dinner. To cap it all off, I see one of the Chinese ladies go up to the angry waitress and tap her to ask a question. The angry waitress at this point screams "DO NOT PUSH ME I DO NOT HAVE A TABLE FOR 5" and all of us just raise our eyebrows.Seriously don't come here. The staff is ridiculous and I've never interacted with such a poor poor example of a waitress ever in my life... yelling at customers is NOT okay.

Name: Caitlin C.
Review: I struggled with this review for a while, but after reflecting on all the places my husband and I visited in Amsterdam, this was ultimately our least favorite.We read so much about Moeder's, including all the fantastic reviews, so we made reservations almost a month in advance. When we finally arrived, we were stared at for a bit in the cramped vestibule of a very crowded (but cozy!) restaurant. When we were seated we were immediately pressured to order all of our courses. When we did order, it took ages for our drinks, and the waitress only returned to deliver our food and settle the bill; no water refills, no drink refills, no eye contact. I understand European service is very different than American service; we repeatedly and politely tried to flag down our waitress but she would literally avoid eye contact and turn around to another table. It was super disheartening and made us very self conscious. All that being said, the food was delicious. I had a beef stew with smashed potatoes and red cabbage, my husband had spare ribs, and we both had speculoos ice cream. Everything tasted great, was plated on adorable vintage china, and the servings were massive. The service, however, left a bad taste in our mouths the entire trip.

Name: Fineprint P.
Review: If you're looking for authentic Dutch food, look no further. My roommate and I were wandering around Amsterdam looking for some lunch, and while we were pondering this place, a man had passed by and said we had definitely come to the right place.The thing about this place is that it's really popular and quite small. We were really lucky to get our seat! Right after us, four groups of 2 people were turned away because they were out of room or the tables open were needed for a later reservation. So if you're planning ahead, make a reservation!The food was really tasty and filling! My roommate and I had shared The Dutch Riceplate, which was a sampler of sorts, and both of us were extremely full afterwards. The food was so tasty!In English, moeders means mothers, and this really showed in the decor of this restaurant. This restaurant celebrates mothers, and they had pictures of mothers lining every inch of their walls.

Name: Erina W.
Review: When I searched for rijsttafel in Amsterdam while planning my trip, I came across a lot of options and narrowed it down to Sampurna. The restaurant has amazing decor and there were several rice table options so I decided to come here to bring my mom and aunt for our first rijsttafel experience. I was concerned at first because we didn't have a reservation and I've read several reviews of being turned away but when we arrived around 5:30-6pm on a Saturday, this place was mainly empty. We were glad to be seated right away and catered to. We really enjoyed the ambiance (totally date night worthy), but found the wait staff to be a little strange. On one hand they can be sweet and offered (to our surprise) that you can have 3 people but order 2 rijsttafel (which was their minimum). Which was really nice and sweet because 2 orders was more than enough for the 3 of us. The food was very filling. But at the same time, the same lady didn't tell us they offer complimentary water, when asked about pricing of bottled water (which I assumed we didn't get free tap water). Either way, it was a very nice experience and we enjoyed the food. However, it was definitely a pricey meal and one I wouldn't probably have again. But if you are to try Indonesian rijsttafel in Amsterdam at least once, this isn't a bad place to try it!

Name: Wendell L.
Review: If you want a feeling of going to Indonesia but don't have the money to go just go eat over here.. the rice table is the one but many different options to chose from..
