Name: Wendell L.
Review: If you want a feeling of going to Indonesia but don't have the money to go just go eat over here.. the rice table is the one but many different options to chose from..

Name: Kailey X.
Review: This place was extremely disappointing. Coming from Malaysia - we were super excited to try an authentic Indonesian restaurant and arrived at 3:20pm because we wanted to skip the dinner crowd. Assuming that we came at an odd hour, we'd be able to be seated, right? Nope. We landed in Amsterdam an hour before and came straight to this restaurant and we were LITERALLY turned away. My friends and I asked for a table of 3 and my friend was told the restaurant is full and to come back later. Seeing that the restaurant was half full with multiple patrons finishing up - I was confused so I went back to the server to ask how long it'd take to be seated. The server told me it'd take one hour - and upon seeing my confused face, gestured to the half empty restaurant (there were only 7 tables with customers - about 50% full) said "Look full! Come back one hour from now and you'll have a seat". It also didn't help that he was literally using his hands to wave me away dismissively as he said that. It didn't make sense at all, because initially when he thought there was only 2, he was happy to seat us- when he realized there were 3 - he said the restaurant is full. None of the tables were reserved either. They had empty dishes waiting to be cleaned up. Another Indonesian family that arrived before us were turned away too. But I didn't see the server treating traditionally western/American looking customers the same way. It was a really off putting experience for the first restaurant we visited in Amsterdam, and I'd never recommend this place to anyone.

Name: Joe G.
Review: Couldn't decide what we wanted for dinner, so I decided to think outside the box.  Apparently Amsterdam is known for these Indonesian Rice Bowl places.  The location was great, close to tram and shopping.  Very easy to find.  We ordered the Celebes Table for two.  Everything was excellent.  My favorites were the goat skewers, the braised beef, and the mango salad.  Word of caution, if you don't do spicy, order something else.  My wife can handle spicy but she needed a break about half way through.  The many small bowls allowed us to try different things without committing to just one dish.  I wish we could have packed this restaurant into our suitcases and taken it home with us.  Now we will start our search for an Indonesian place near home.

Name: Rosemary V.
Review: We walked in on a weekday evening and we're quickly seated even though we did not have reservationsThe good: -Place is super cute and intimate- Food: We had the Kuning rice Table for four and the food was more than enough.All the dishes were super yummy and I like that there was a variety of dishes for all dietary needs.- Service was good.- Prices were reasonableThe bad: I can't think of anythingFinal verdict: One of our best meals in Amsterdam. I would certainly return.

Name: Marilyn T.
Review: I kind of had my heart set on the Indonesian rice table experience, and this place had fairly good ratings, but we ended up walking out.It was very poor service and communication about seating. There was just one guy there for the front of the house, and he didn't seem to care whether we ate there or not. The front part of the restaurant was fairly full during lunch around 12:30pm on a Sunday, so I get that he was busy, but we just got a very clear sense that our business didn't matter to him.

Name: Edward W.
Review: This restaurant is located right next to the flower market and seems pretty nondescript from the outside. Dropped by for lunch and it was pretty much empty. I ordered the fried rice which tasted quite good and was slightly salty. My friend ordered the chicken soup which smelled great, but ended up being very light in flavor. He loved it since he wanted something more bland.There were also several shared small plates in the middle. A basic cucumber dish, fried egg in curry sauce, shrimp crackers, and sweet and sour nuts. We never got a chance to see if they refill these plates, but each one was quite good.

Name: David S.
Review: Too tight and slow service. The food is just average. Wanted dessert and was told the kitchen was closed. I'd try another Indonesia place.

Name: Anju J.
Review: The worst restaurant in our entire Europe trip.Horrible servicethey don't give tap water until you order a beverage- then why do i need water?For that price of meal, this cheapness ruins thingsThe food doesn't stand out. One person in our party was vegetarian and they got 4-5 tofu dishes, bit much..lacking creativityDo not recommend at all

Name: Amy C.
Review: The Indonesian food here was so-so. Our entire table felt it was overpriced and not very good. The worst part is that our waiter lied to us by telling us we needed to buy a bottled water and could not get tap water. Then we saw later that nearby tables had carafes of tap water. We also waited quite a long time to order and get our check. By the end, we were very eager to leave. I would not recommend this place!

Name: Adrian K.
Review: Overall : Service is bad, food is not authentic (I grew up eating Indonesian food) and pricey. Experience: I asked for hot sambal and the waitress replied "the sauce on the food is spicy enough" and walked away. Further, we have to ask a few times for water and finally got the jug of water but with no glasses to drink with. At the end, she explicitly asked for tip when we were paying. Would never come back considering how many good Indonesian food options in Amsterdam.

Name: TS R.
Review: Ok. If you want the authentic Dutch experience you can't get any better. Can't wait to return in May 2023.

Name: Yixuan S.
Review: We saw this restaurant recommended on a YouTube video.  It showed  hearty winter sustaining food described as typical home-made dishes from Dutch cuisine.  It lived up to its reputation and was just what we needed on our cold November Day.  The restaurant is located on the heavily touristed Leidsekruisstraat and we feared that we wouldn't get in without a reservation.  Luckily a table of two inside by the front window was just opening up as we arrived and the waiter kindly gave it to us.  Whew!  Not only did we get a table, but in my mind, we got the best table of all.  Out of the 4 3-course menu options we chose Menu 1 which was very reasonable priced at 21.50 Euros per person. Course one was pea soup (with pieces of sausage) with rye bread with cheese and mustard.  The second course was sausage (or meatball) and three sides which are in Dutch 'hutspot, boerenkoolstamppot and zuurkoolstamppot.'  But in English these are 1. mashed potatoes mixed with sauerkraut, 2. mashed potatoes mixed with broccoli, and 3. mashed potatoes mixed with carrots and herbs. All three were delicious.  And surprisingly we both ate it all.  Luckily the dessert of vanilla custard with yogurt and a fruit syrup was light, although tasty.  The food was delivered incredibly quickly since this menu is extremely popular.   But in truth all the service was very professional: fast, efficient, and very friendly.  Their were other menu choices that we would have loved to try, and had we stayed in Amsterdam longer I'm sure we would have returned.  In this city of international cuisine we were glad to find typical Dutch fare, excellently made and presented.

Name: Johanna S.
Review: Should be 1 star but friendly service 2 stars. Food here is atrocious, the worst restaurant I've had in Amsterdam by a LONG SHOT. Any menu with multiple languages is likely horrendous. Against intuition, i came anyhow wanting "local dutch"Large portions, fried, low quality ingredients. Go elsewhere.  It's also not cheap.THE FOOD:- bread: not good, crusty, or homemade- fish platter: smoked eel, tiny shrimp and herring.  Herring almost made me throw up lol texture was awful - goat cheese salad: couldn't eat, goat cheese was too strong - sea bass: weirdly textured, served with buttered boiled (frozen?) vegetables- mashed potatoes: microwaved? Hard on the outside, soft on the inside - mini pancakes: highlight of the meal. Only thing I really ate TLDR: do not come here! Unless you only come for pancakes. Lolll

Name: Jackson S.
Review: There are a lot of choices to eat around here. Across the street is Italian that boasts "it's simply the best" and the place outside with a rowdy table has Dutch mussels and fries for 10 euros. So, why come here? Well, Yelp says it's good Dutch traditional food. It looks cute inside, may be 1930s style with porcelain plates and tassled fake candelabras on the wall, despite it only being open since 2000.As with all traditional restaurants, The Pantry does a bustling tourist trade. Is that good or bad? Neither. Everyone's having fun, and they welcome lone diners like me. In fact I even lucked out and got a window table on a pleasant late summer night ( no rain, 60F). If you don't might the occasional waft of cigarettes coming into your meal it's a nice spot.I ordered combo of hutspot (mashed potato with beef and veg) boerenkoolstamppot (mashed potato, kale and bacon) and zuurkoolstamppot (mashed potato with sauerkraut). It was tasty, although a bit salty, esp the bacon dish. I got the yogurt and custard dessert which was as it sounded. An odd combo, but tasty. You're supposed to mix it together, but I ate it separately.All, in all a nicer dining experience than the other places in this area. The host / server was really friendly and humorous. The place as packed. I tried another Dutch restaurant in another part of town and it was better, but more expensive.

Name: Joshua B.
Review: The pantryI came here with my husband to try out some Dutch food. We ordered the special #1 and #2. Menu 1:Pea soup - good, but not spectacular or special in any way. 3 mounds - they had certain flavors such as sauerkraut, kale, and one other one. They were decent. Vlaflip - my husband described it as dannon yogurt. And he's kinda right. :/ there was nothing really special about it Menu 2:Goat cheese croquettes - these were actually good, and I don't like goat cheese. Guess that's what happens when you deep fry anything though Ground beef, cauliflower, and mashed potatoes - just like shepherds pie. It was actually kinda bland, but it felt healthy due to the cauliflower. Really filling. Poffertjes aka mini pancakes - was the highlight of our mealOverall I would say that 1) the decor is cool 2) it's a very touristy restaurant 3) the food overall wasn't that good / maybe I'm just not super into Dutch food. 4) service was quite slow5) maybe was a bit overpriced for what it was I would not actually recommend this place. Also the fact that cigarette smoke from the outside kept coming in was very bothersome

Name: Viet L.
Review: Eh, this place was okay.Came here on my first night in Amsterdam since I was starving and got a table in a small, but packed, restaurant. I didn't know what to order so I got an item on the traditional Dutch section of the menu.Turns out it was 3 different types of mash and a sausage. It was interesting and a completely different flavour profile than I'm used to but it wasn't anything to write home about (but Yelp is a different story lol)Maybe I need to try something else, or maybe Dutch food isn't my thing.

Name: Shannon W.
Review: Where to begin! I am in love with the food here.The waitresses are friendly and with the cozy indoor ambiance, I'm sure to come back with a group of friends. Groups of four-six can expect at longer wait.We ordered the cheese fondue, menu option A (sea bass) and the combination platter (). Cheese fondue with brown and white bread, tomato slices, cucumbers and a side salad The waitress exclaimed "Wow you finished your food. Completely finished it." That's how it went down!

Name: Fiona H.
Review: Very disappointed after seeing the other high reviews.Food was standard tourist fare, not authentically Dutch or special in any way.Service was truly horrible, as opposed to the many other friendly restaurants in the area.To top it all off, they added an item to my bill I never ordered or had. They manually reduced the amount when I pointed it out, without any sort of apology or even smile.

Name: Doug A.
Review: We had a wonderful early dinner at The Pantry, we were lucky to get a table since they are usually so busy. The service was great and the food was perfectly traditional Dutch food- would definitely return

Name: Monica D.
Review: The restaurant is k own for their Dutch traditional meals.  The beef stew  entree is delicious.. lots of great flavors.  The fish entree was okay... there wasn't much flavor so I would recommend getting their traditional entrees.  The desserts- mousse and chocolate ice cream and Carmel ice cream were delicious.  If you want to go for dinner, you should definitely make a reservation if you eat after 7;00 pm.

Name: Neluta G.
Review: Unfortunately this place did not impress. I was excited about it but it was disappointing. The dish I had "duck" not very good and they were kind enough to take it off the bill. I did explain that I do not care about that, I only care about the food experience but the guy that it is in charge of the menu insisted.The restaurant has these beautiful chandeliers, it brings you back to a Victorian era.Wine was OK, service was good. Lot's of restaurants in Amsterdam so...... there are many other choices.

Name: Rose Z.
Review: Location: Address is Spuistraat 3a, 1012 SP Amsterdam, Netherlands. However the restaurant has two doors: one is on the Spuistraat and another facing Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. Reservation: you may reserve it early on The TripAdvisor via TheFork. You can call the restaurant to make a last-minute reservation.Setting: semi-formal and nicely decoratedService: professional and friendlyFood: well-prepared, good in taste and presentation. A stater and two main dishes were orderedESCARGOTS € 11.50 (starter), strongly recommended (We had Escargots at South France several times during this trip, but this one is simply the BEST).EENDENBOUT € 22.50, (duck-leg, main dish), 4.5 starNOORDZEE TONG € 34, (Dutch sole), 5 starThe best restaurant experience in this Amsterdam trip!

Name: Shelby R.
Review: Really disappointed. The service was just terrible, I really wish I remember the name of the woman waiter who took care of my boyfriend and I. She acted like she had better things to do and very snobby. We both had the seafood risotto which was good. We just couldn't get over how horrible the service was. Mind you we are a very easy table, no substitution or extras. Just be pleasant and nice and we will have a great time. We still wonder how someone could be so rude to people who just wanted a good meal. Oh well. Other people seem to have a good experience here, I recommend if you go to go cautiously.

Name: Nola G.
Review: I wanted to try this restaurant because a foodie friend(who likes most of my favorite restaurants in Paris) highly recommended Van Speyk. I promised him that I would eat here.  The restaurant is very pretty. I just felt the prices where too high for the quality of the food, execution of the dishes, and service that I received. I tried to Dutch Sole (Noordzeetong) which I felt I could have prepared as equally-well at home. The Van Speyk salad sounded delicious but it was also lackluster. The menu is fabulous. I was interested in the seafood risotto. When I was informed it came in a bought ore-made mix, that should have been my heads-up. I was in the mood for a dinner that "wowed" on a cold winter holiday night. Unfortunately, it didn't happen and I couldn't even stick around for dessert. The restaurant was empty.  Another couple showed an hour after opening. vanspeyk.amsterdam

Name: Tim K.
Review: Read all the great reviews and I concur. Great atmosphere, service was great, and the food was even better. Couldn't recommend the place more. I want to venture out to the rest of Amsterdam this week but I will definitely be back here

Name: Katherine P.
Review: Made a reservation on open table which I'm glad I did since the restaurant was extremely busy.  The menu had various Dutch dishes and were easily marked on the menu. Food was fabulous but service was extremely too slow.   We sat outside which wa
